articles.title: Will Spain's housing crisis lead to a snap election?
articles.summary: The BBC's Guy Hedgecoe is in Madrid, where a series of marches have been scheduled, after Spain's Congress rejected measures aimed at tackling the country's housing crisis.
articles.body:
Thousands of people are continuing protests across Spain, after Congress rejected a series of measures aimed at tackling the country's housing crisis.

Lawmakers voted on two decree-laws presented by government in response to nationwide protests that followed the eviction of 87-year-old Maricarmen Abascal from her home.

Abascal was evicted after she was unable to pay a rent increase by the company that owns her flat. The case triggered a broader movement across the country demanding affordable rentals, which have soared in recent years.

The BBC's Guy Hedgecoe is at one of the protests in Madrid and looks at whether the government's defeat will lead to an early general election, which is not due until next summer.

articles.title: Tech layoffs tracker 2026: All the job losses across Xbox, Apple, Oracle, Uber, TikTok, Meta and others
articles.summary: We're more than half way through the year, and there have already been more than 190,000 layoffs across the tech industry — here's what we know.
articles.body:
We've been inundated with tech layoffs throughout the whole of 2026 — and there's likely more to come. In June, 14,000 job cuts happened at EV automaker Lucid, game developer Bungie, trading platform company Robinhood and others. Microsoft 's latest round of layoffs happened shortly after, affecting 4,800 jobs — mostly across its Xbox gaming division. Following that, companies like Samsung, Zillow and even TikTok joined the club.

According to many reports , the U.S. is at the center of these job cuts. Oracle has had the biggest impact on layoffs this year so far. The annual financial disclosure the company filed on June 23 showed the software giant cut 21,000 jobs over the past year, roughly 13% of its workforce.

"The adoption and deployment of AI technologies across our operations have resulted, and may continue to result, in reductions to our workforce," Oracle said in the filing.

In response to the numerous job cuts, California Governor Gavin Newsom in June unveiled a tool to track AI's impact on the workforce . "As AI advances, we aren't just watching from the sidelines; we're reimagining how we prepare California through strong governance and innovative policy." And recently, more than 4,500 Google workers signed a petition calling for layoff protections as things get worse. Some of the protections they're asking for include buyouts before mandatory layoffs and guaranteed severance.

TrueUp finds that layoffs seem to be moving at a faster rate than last year — over 245,000 workers in tech were let go in 2025, while there have been more than 185,000 layoffs in 2026 so far. Several of the companies below have laid off employees due to increased spending in AI. We'll get into the reasons for the layoffs.

Xbox announced it eliminated 268 roles across Halo Studios, other first-party studios and additional areas of the Xbox Game Studios division. These layoffs are part of a "reset" it announced this summer; the company already laid off 1,600 people in July, and said at the time that an additional 1,600 terminations were still to come.

According to a Bloomberg report , Apple has laid off an undisclosed number of employees from Fitness+, the company's exercise subscription service. According to the report, the layoffs affected those who worked in the audio side of the division, which includes features like Time to Walk and Time to Run guided audio workouts. Reportedly, offerings like this will be reduced — but not eliminated completely — from the service.

Oracle employees were impacted by yet another round of layoffs in September. The total number of employees laid off this time around is not currently known. The tech giant reportedly set employees early morning emails on Monday, September 14, letting those affected know it would be their last working day. It's also reported that, with these layoffs, Oracle is looking to offset the amount of money is pouring into AI chips and data centers. Earlier this year, Oracle laid off 21,000 people.

Uber announced it will cut 3,300 jobs, or about 10% of its workforce, in a big restructuring effort. "We are removing layers, simplifying team structures, refining our global location strategy, and focusing our people and investments against the biggest opportunities ahead of us," CEO Dara Khosrowshahi said in a statement . While the cuts apply to both regular employees and managers, the company stated it will reduce the "number of employees who sit 7+ layers from the CEO" by 20%, and it will cut the number of "micro-teams" by almost 50%. The CEO's memo did not mention AI as catalyst for the layoffs, but it did explain that this restructuring will allow Uber to bring its services to more people, invest in more drivers and merchants and "build the autonomous future."

According to an AppleInsider report , Apple laid off at least 60 people in its Vision Group, which is the team responsible for the Vision Pro VR headset. A Bloomberg report notes that Apple is also laying off roles in its Intelligent Systems Experience group, which is partially responsible for some of the AI systems on Apple devices. Overall, its estimated the layoffs affect more than 200 people.

When it comes to Vision Group and Vision Pro, it's been reported that incoming CEO John Ternus would be putting that product category "on ice," so this seems like the start of that process. The Vision Pro headset came out in 2024 with an eye-watering $3,699 starting price, and it remains to be seen if Apple will be pulling out of the AR/VR category entirely in the future. The Intelligence Systems changes are reportedly tied to changes that are necessary for the technical architecture for Apple's newly AI-infused Siri.

The New York Times reported that TikTok will lay off 250 people and close its Nashville, Tennessee office in October. This location was home to, in part, some of TikTok's content moderation team, although the company has not specified the reason for the layoffs or which teams they primarily affect. "We have decided to close our Nashville office to streamline our operations and better align our teams for long-term growth," a press officer for what is known as the TikTok U.S.D.S. Joint Venture said in a statement to the Times.

Zillow will lay off just over 500 people as it enacts organizational changes across the company. "These are difficult decisions that reflect both the strides we're making in our strategy and the reality of what is required of us to grow at scale," CEO Jeremy Wacksman wrote in a press release . Wacksman didn't go into detail about what organizational changes were made, or which departments are bearing the brunt of the layoffs. "These changes are about ensuring we have a disciplined cost structure and getting more efficient, with the right people in the right positions," he wrote.

Etsy laid off about 220 people, or 12% of its workforce, as it attempts to simplify its organizational structure. The cuts primarily affected the product and engineering teams, and Etsy CEO Kruti Patel Goyal said that the layoffs were necessary to build "the organization we believe Etsy needs for the future." An Etsy spokesperson told CNBC that the cuts were not driven by artificial intelligence adoption.

Microsoft has begun another round of layoffs that affects 4,800 jobs , or around 2.1% of its workforce. The Xbox division is getting hit the hardest, with 3,200 roles getting cut through fiscal year 2027, Xbox chief Asha Sharma said in a post on X — 1,600 people were let go on July 6. Shortly after those layoffs were revealed, it was announced that Sharma was appointed to a U.S. Federal Reserve task force to help advise it on "productivity and jobs." Other appointees include Marc Andreessen of Andreessen Horowitz and Charles I. Jones, professor of economics at Stanford University.

Intel is reportedly downsizing its data center group, despite strong performance. The company hasn't disclosed how many roles would be affected.

Visa will be cutting about 2,600 jobs, which amounts to about 7% of its workforce. The layoffs will primarily affect the technology and product teams, and the impetus in part is to make the company more efficient. "To capture the opportunities ahead and best position Visa to lead this transformation, we must continue evolving how we work," Chief Executive Officer Ryan McInerney wrote in a memo. "AI is also helping to accelerate this evolution and shape the way work gets done at Visa." But according to Bloomberg's report, AI was not the only factor to influence Visa's decision to do these layoffs. The company reportedly intends to reinvest in things like consumer payments and value-added services like stablecoin.

Software company Monday.com will be laying off 20% of its workforce, which comes out to about 630 people. This comes as the company makes a pivot to AI and is attempting to make its AI platform a core offering of its business. Earlier this year, it designed its main product around the idea that business customers increasingly want its employees to work with AI agents.

Patreon laid off 20% of its workforce, or 93 people, as a result of the company "changing our organizational structure and how we work." But Patreon was explicit in its email to creators and staff that "we are not making the above changes because we believe AI replaces humans." However, the email also said "AI has fundamentally transformed the tech industry, though, including how we work."

Uber has reportedly laid off 10% of its customer service division, according to a Bloomberg report, as it looks to "embrace artificial intelligence" and simplify its ranks. The company also stated in May that it would slow hiring as it makes use of AI more internally.

Samsung is eliminating 179 jobs as it moves its New Jersey headquarters to Texas later this year. The move is expected to impact around 1,000 workers. We're now getting a fuller picture of what that looks like: according to Reuters , 739 roles at Samsung's New Jersey location have been affected in some way. Some have been offered relocation packages as the company shifts its headquarters to Texas, while others have been let go. In addition, it's reported that 100 roles in its Texas location, primarily in the mobile division, have also been let go.

Amazon will lay off some people in its artificial general intelligence group, although the company has not disclosed how many roles will be affected. "This is a fast-moving space, and we're sharpening our focus on the initiatives that matter most for customers, so we can move faster on what counts," an Amazon spokesperson told CNBC.

Sony Interactive Entertainment released a statement that it's cutting "a significant number of employees" from its Bungie workforce. That includes most of the Destiny team and some Marathon team members, as well as SIE teams that support Bungie's operations. The email didn't say how many employees were affected.

Electric vehicle maker Lucid announced it's cutting around 18% of its workforce, and also noted COO Marc Winterhoff's leaving the company, Reuters reported . The layoffs are in an effort to "​boost profitability amid growing competition." The cuts affect full-time employees, contractors and hourly manufacturing workers.

Cloud computing services company Rackspace laid off 750 workers , or around 15% of its workforce. The cuts are driven by a shift in focus toward AI.

EV company Rivian let go of hundreds of employees , which amounts to around 2% of the company's workforce, the Wall Street Journal reported . Those affected were part of Rivian's service and customer organization, which handled marketing and sales.

Trading platform company Robinhood is planning to lay off 10% of its staff to restructure, the Robinhood Comms account shared on X today — that's around 290 jobs. It's unclear if the layoffs are AI-related, but CEO Vlad Tenev noted the company will be "utilizing frontier technologies to push our execution even further."

Salesforce laid off at least 86 employees in California, though Business Insider sources say job cuts also occurred in Washington and outside the U.S. as well. The cuts reportedly affect employees involved with Salesforce's Agentforce AI product, Mulesoft IT integration tool and its Marketing Cloud software.

Groupon is planning to lay off roughly 25% of its workforce , which will result in 400 job cuts. Those positions are expected to be eliminated by the end of the third quarter. This is in an effort to restructure the company and rebuild it as an AI-native company.

In another set of AI-related layoffs, website builder Wix said it was cutting around 20% of staff. Wix cofounder and CEO Avishai Abrahami announced the cuts on X , pointing to the changes AI is bringing to the industry and stating "we need to become a faster, leaner, and flatter organization." He also put part of the blame on the Israeli Shekel to U.S. Dollar exchange rates, which impact the company because it's based in Israel. The cuts are expected to impact around 1,000 roles, based on Wix's headcount.

Webflow, a website builder and hosting company, conducted a round of layoffs that an employee called "a bloodbath" in a statement to the San Francisco Chronicle . It's unclear how many employees were impacted, but one anonymous developer from the company told the Chronicle they believe it was larger than Webflow's last major round of layoffs, which affected 8% of its workforce in 2024. As with other recent layoffs, it looks like a shift to AI is to blame here. "AI is rewriting the rules for how marketing teams create, test, and optimize digital experiences," CEO Linda Tong said in a statement . "And the companies that move decisively through moments like this are the ones that come out ahead."

ClickUp CEO Zeb Evans announced that the company cut 22% of its workforce as it turns toward AI to improve productivity. He claimed it "wasn't about cutting costs," but about funneling savings from the cuts "directly back into the people who stay." The company has introduced million-dollar salary bands reserved for employees who "create outsized impact using AI."

Intuit is planning to lay off 3,000 employees, or about 17% of its workforce, Reuters reports . CEO Sasan Goodarzi sent a memo to employees noting the layoffs would help the company's efforts of focusing on infusing AI across its services.

Meta has officially begun cutting 10% of its workforce , totaling around 8,000 employees. In addition, it plans to close 6,000 open roles. The reason is to allow more room for AI spending.

Like Microsoft, NPR is offering voluntary buyouts to 300 employees in the newsroom, but only 30 will be accepted. However, if the news organization doesn't receive its target number, it will result in targeted layoffs. The reason is due to the loss of federal funding.

The online retail giant cut more jobs this month, this time from the Selling Partner Services organization. These new layoffs come after Amazon cut roughly 30,000 jobs in rounds across October and January. A spokesperson told Business Insider that the most recent layoffs have affected a "small number" of employees. The Selling Partner Services team works with third-party merchants on Amazon, providing onboarding, logistics and account management support.

Cisco is cutting just under 4,000 jobs in Q4, CEO Chuck Robbins said in a blog post . Impacted employees will receive pro-rated payment of 2026 bonuses and will also receive "support in finding new opportunities" via Cisco's placement services. In June, it was confirmed that the layoffs include 471 workers in the Bay Area .

"While we are reducing roles in some areas, we are making clear, strategic investments — particularly in silicon, optics, security, and in our employees' use of AI across the company," Robbins said.

LinkedIn is planning to lay off 5% of its staff, which is around 875 employees, Reuters reports . An anonymous person told Reuters the reason is to reorganize teams and focus employees on areas ⁠where its business is growing. However, one of the sources said the reason was "not for artificial intelligence to replace jobs at LinkedIn."

GM is letting go of around 500 to 600 employees in the Information Technology sector, Bloomberg reports . The reason is to "trim costs and clear the way to bring in staff with skills in other technology areas."

Due to restructuring driven by AI, Cloudflare is cutting more than 1,100 employees . "Today's actions are not a cost-cutting exercise or an assessment of individuals' performance; They are about Cloudflare defining how a world-class, high-growth company operates and creates value in the agentic AI era," Prince and President Michelle Zatlyn said in an email to employees .

PayPal is planning to cut around 20% of its staff — nearly 4,800 employees — over the next few years, according to the Wall Street Journal . "First, we will remove duplication and layers from our organizational structure. Second, we will accelerate our AI adoption and automation across our operations," CEO Enrique Lores said to investors.

Cryptocurrency platform Coinbase is laying off 700 employees , which amounts to around 14% of its staff. CEO Brian Armstrong cites the current market and AI changing the way they work as reasons for the layoffs.

Microsoft is offering a first-ever buyout to up to 7% of its employees, CNBC reports . It's a one-time retirement program that's available for workers at the senior director level and below whose years of employment and age are 70 or higher.

Nike announced it's laying off 1,400 people this week. "Collectively, these changes will result in a reduction of approximately 1,400 roles in global operations, with the majority in technology," COO Venkatesh Alagirisamy said. "These reductions are very hard for the teammates directly affected and for the teams around them, too."

Amazon is planning to temporarily close a warehouse in Homestead, Florida, which will eliminate more than 600 jobs, Newsweek reports . The job cuts will start in July and continue through September but the giant company is giving employees the option to relocate to other facilities. The warehouse has only been open for just under two years but Amazon is already looking to update the site.

Battery recycling company Redwood Materials laid off 10% of its employees, totaling 135 people, TechCrunch reports . Those who were let go received an email from the chief HR officer telling them the layoffs were made "to sharpen our focus, our work and the size of our teams to support the direction Redwood is going in the future."

Snap is laying off 1,000 workers , which is 16% of its staff, Variety reports . The Snapchat parent company made the announcement just weeks after Irenic Capital Management asked the company to make changes to improve performance and revenue.

Snap is using AI to streamline operations and assist the now smaller workforce. "We have already witnessed small squads leveraging AI tools to drive meaningful progress across several important initiatives," Snap CEO Evan Spiegel said.

Just two months after taking over as CEO of Disney, Josh D'Amaro announced the company is laying off 1,000 of its employees, AP News reports . In addition, Marvel let 8% of its staff go after the call was made.

"Over the past several months, we have looked at ways in which we can streamline our operations in various parts of the company to ensure we deliver the world-class creativity and innovation our fans value and expect from Disney," D'Amaro said in a memo to employees. "Given the fast-moving pace of our industries, this requires us to constantly assess how to foster a more agile and technologically-enabled workforce to meet tomorrow's needs."

The wearable camera maker this year will eliminate 145 employees due to a restructuring plan to cut costs, the Wall Street Journal reported . The cuts are expected to last until the end of the year.

Vimeo is going through its third round of layoffs since it was acquired by Bending Spoons. This time, the company let go of more than 120 people, which is about 25% of its city staff .

It's been reported that 200 Meta employees in the Bay Area will lose their jobs at the end of May. That includes 124 employees in Burlingame and 74 in Sunnyvale. The company last laid off workers just a few weeks ago.

Oracle has begun implementing a big cull of its employee base . On the final day of March, more than a dozen Oracle employees announced on LinkedIn they had been let go from their jobs, Business Insider reports . It's unclear at this time how many workers were affected, but it was projected to be thousands at the start of this month.

Those laid off received the same email : "After careful consideration of Oracle's current business needs, we have made the decision to eliminate your role as part of a broader organizational change."

The job cuts are reportedly to help Oracle stem a cash drain related its expenditures on AI infrastructure. In June, Oracle revealed that it had laid off 21,000 people as part of the cuts.

Deux Ex studio Eidos-Montréal announced on March 30 that it's laying off 124 people . In response, the studio head David Anfossi has decided to leave the company.

The cuts are a result of "changing project needs and impacts across production and support teams," the gaming company said in a LinkedIn post . It also noted that the decision to lay off these employees is not related to their talent or performance.

After already having layoffs in January , T-Mobile has cut even more of its workers, GeekWire reports . It's unclear how many people were laid off at this time, but it could be in the hundreds.

"To move even faster in a dynamic market while continuing to deliver best-in-class digital experiences for our customers, we're further aligning our IT organization to support future growth and innovation… This includes the difficult decision of eliminating some roles while continuing to invest and hire in areas," T-Mobile told GeekWire in a statement.

Meta began laying off hundreds of employees on March 25, totaling around 700 people, per The New York Times . Those impacted were part of the Reality Labs team, as well as social media and recruiting teams. Though still significant, this is a much smaller number compared to a Reuters report that suggested 20% off staff would be affected by layoffs due to the increased spending on AI.

This change comes as the company is shifting away from its metaverse creation, which includes Horizon Worlds for its Quest VR headset that's operated by the Reality Labs team.

The gaming giant on March 24 announced it was laying off more than 1,000 workers in an effort to right-size the staff of its popular free-to-play online shooter, Fortnite. CEO Tim Sweeney sent a note to his staff, citing the reason for the layoffs is due to the "downturn in Fortnite engagement," which means "we're spending significantly more than we're making, and we have to make major cuts to keep the company funded." He made it a point to note the layoffs are not related to AI.

105 employees from the Red Storm Entertainment team were laid off by Ubisoft in an effort to cut costs, IGN reports . Game development has ended at the studio, so the downsizing will remain permanent. The company employed 180 people in 2022 but has seen multiple layoffs over the years.

Roughly 1,600 employees were laid off at Atlassian on March 16, which is around 10% of total workers. Ahead of the layoffs, Atlassian CEO Mike Cannon-Brookes shared a message with the entire team, letting them know the reason is to "self-fund further investment in AI and enterprise sales, while strengthening our financial profile. We're also changing the way we work and reorganising around our System of Work to move faster." Impacted employees received an email shortly after this message went out.

articles.title: Buried 120 years under sands of time, fraying paper puts Bhander’s railway dream back on track
articles.summary: Bhander rail link demand gains momentum after 1905-06 Gwalior-era gazette surfaces, reviving Jhansi-Bhind line plan and fueling citizen campaign in Datia.
articles.body: BHOPAL: Written and published 120 years ago, it lay as a yellowing and forgotten scrap of paper, buried in the sands of time. However, the old document, dating back to the Gwalior Riyasat era, proposing a railway link between Jhansi and Bhind, is now driving a public campaign for a connectivity push at Bhander in Madhya Pradesh’s Datia district, one that locals believe could also open up new commercial opportunities.Mentioned in a 1905-06 railway gazette from the Gwalior Riyasat era and preserved in a 1996 reprint, the fraying document was found among the papers in possession of former minister and Congress MLA Keshari Chowdhary (80), who obtained the reprint while raising a question in the assembly in 1996.Chowdhary confirmed that the document clearly mentions a proposed Jhansi-Bhind railway line. “I received a copy of the reprint of the old gazette of 1905, which was reprinted in 1996 during an assembly reply. It clearly mentions a proposed Jhansi-Bhind railway line,” Chowdhary told TOI.The discovery has given fresh momentum to a citizen-driven push for railway connectivity that began as informal discussions among traders, youth and other residents about Bhander’s lack of public transport.A ‘Rail Lao Abhiyan’ has now convened two meetings, with residents planning village-to-village outreach and formation of a committee to take the demand forward.“Bhander is growing into a big town and there are several places of religious significance nearby. Every month, about 20,000-25,000 people come visiting this place, but public transport leaves plenty to be desired. After 4.30pm, there is hardly any commuting option apart from private vehicles if you want to travel outside Bhander,” Manish Poddar, a 51-year-old foodgrain trader, told TOI.He said traders had initially discussed a railway link between Chirgaon and Datia, which would have put Bhander on the national railway network. “Then we found the old gazette. It showed that the railway line proposed earlier could be more viable for Bhander,” Poddar said.Bhander is also a foodgrain warehousing hub but lacks a railway loading facility, Poddar said, estimating that such a facility could potentially generate Rs 25 crore to Rs 50 crore in railway revenue.Yuvraj Chowdhary (45), son of the former Congress minister, said the document has changed the campaign’s course. “The demand was put forward very casually for a start, with only a few people discussing it. However, more people joined with time, turning into a public campaign. Initially, we were discussing a separate railway line. But after chancing upon the old document, we realised that the line it proposes is significantly better and more feasible for Bhander. We are now in the process of generating greater public awareness about it,” Yuvraj said.The campaign is being projected as a non-political citizen initiative. “More than 800 people have joined our cause through our social media groups and at least 100-150 are actively pursuing it. Now we will meet and take it up with our local MP (BJP’s Sandhya Ray from Bhind Lok Sabha constituency),” Poddar said.The second campaign meeting could see further intensification of village-level outreach before the movement’s next course is set.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Bhopal | Silver Rate in Bhopal | Bank Holidays in Bhopal | Public Holidays in Bhopal | Petrol Price in Bhopal | Diesel Price in Bhopal | CNG Price in Bhopal | LPG Price in BhopalStay updated with the latest Bhopal news. articles.title: US Coast Guard says it seized Cuba-bound ships with thousands of gallons of oil
articles.summary: Video shows Coast Guard agents equipped in tactical gear boarding the ship.
articles.body:
The U.S. Coast Guard announced on Friday the seizure of two ships bound for Cuba that were illegally carrying thousands of gallons of diesel fuel amid the ongoing fuel blockade to the country imposed by President Donald Trump.

The "Grace," a 300-foot tanker, was seized on Sept. 5 by the Coast Guard and Mexican authorities in the Caribbean Sea between Cuba and Mexico, after it was alleged to use covert operations to traverse the high seas, according to Coast Guard officials. Another ship, carrying 200,000 gallons of fuel, was seized by the Coast Guard in June.

The ships' seizures came amid the Trump administration's fuel blockade on Cuba. That move, aimed at trying to force changes to Cuba's political system, has led to a power crisis in Cuba, marked by prolonged power outages impacting water supply, lighting, refrigeration and communications, according to U.S. officials.

The Grace was brought to Progreso, Mexico, "where a Mexican Navy (MARINA) inspection team confirmed the presence of large quantities of fuel in the vessel's ballast tanks," according to a news release from the Coast Guard.

Video first obtained by ABC News shows Coast Guard agents equipped in tactical gear boarding the ship, guns drawn, while a separate Coast Guard boat goes alongside of it.

The Coast Guard also announced the seizure of another Cuba-bound ship, the "Jaira Provider," which they say was carrying more than 200,000 gallons of fuel when it was seized on June 28.

The Coast Guard said that the fuel in the Jaria Provider was also stored in ballast tanks, which are typically used to hold water or air to control the ship's buoyancy.

"The high seas are not a sanctuary for lawlessness," said Adm. Kevin Lunday, commandant of the Coast Guard. "Dark fleet actors who employ deceptive tactics to engage in illicit activities will not evade justice. The Coast Guard is bringing every capability to bear to interdict these vessels and uphold international law."

articles.title: Protestos liderados pela geração Z contra cadastro eleitoral da Índia terminam com detenções | G1
articles.standfirst: Grupo de jovens e organizações de oposição acusam governo de Narendra Modi de favorecer seu partido com alterações no cadastro de eleitores e pede renúncia do chefe da Comissão Eleitoral.
articles.summary: Grupo de jovens e organizações de oposição acusam governo de Narendra Modi de favorecer seu partido com alterações no cadastro de eleitores e pede renúncia do chefe da Comissão Eleitoral.
articles.body:
Manifestante usa máscara com o rosto do primeiro-ministro indiano, Narendra Modi, durante protesto que pede a renúncia do presidente da Comissão Eleitoral da Índia, Gyanesh Kumar, em Nova Délhi, em 3 de outubro de 2026. — Foto: REUTERS/Adnan Abidi

A polícia indiana deteve várias pessoas neste sábado (3), segundo uma fonte policial, durante o segundo dia de protestos em Nova Délhi contra mudanças no cadastro de eleitores do país .

As manifestações são apoiadas pelo Cockroach Janta Party, grupo político ligado à geração Z , e por outras organizações de oposição.

Os participantes afirmam que as alterações favorecem o partido do primeiro-ministro Narendra Modi e pedem a renúncia do presidente da Comissão Eleitoral da Índia, Gyanesh Kumar.

👉 Os protestos são os mais recentes de uma série de manifestações lideradas por jovens que surgiram neste ano e aumentaram a pressão sobre Modi, que está no poder há 12 anos .

Cerca de 100 manifestantes retiraram barreiras de segurança neste sábado e gritaram palavras de ordem como "ladrão de votos, deixe o cargo" e "Gyanesh Kumar, renuncie". Policiais detiveram à força parte do grupo.

O parlamentar independente Kapil Sibal, a presidente da All India Students' Association, Neha Bora, e os ativistas políticos Prashant Bhushan e Yogendra Yadav estavam entre os manifestantes, segundo uma testemunha da Reuters.

A polícia não informou quantas pessoas foram detidas nem suas identidades.

"Primeiro, retiraram pessoas da lista de eleitores e agora não estão nos deixando protestar contra isso. Isso é inaceitável", disse Bora à Reuters.

Kumar não comentou os protestos nem os pedidos para que deixe o cargo.

Na sexta-feira (2), a polícia impediu outro grupo de manifestantes de se reunir e colocou vários deles em ônibus. Estações de metrô próximas permaneceram fechadas devido ao forte esquema de segurança.

Embora muitas das pessoas detidas na sexta-feira tenham sido liberadas, várias foram acusadas de supostamente desrespeitar ordens que proíbem grandes aglomerações em Nova Délhi, segundo uma fonte policial.

Os protestos estão relacionados a um processo nacional de verificação do cadastro eleitoral iniciado no ano passado. Críticos afirmam que a medida levou à retirada de milhões de eleitores que teriam direito a votar.

A Comissão Eleitoral, uma instituição que por muito tempo esteve entre as mais confiáveis da Índia, afirma que a revisão tem como objetivo retirar do cadastro eleitores duplicados, pessoas que morreram e pessoas que não atendem aos requisitos para votar.

Na sexta-feira, o órgão determinou que fossem cadastrados novos eleitores que passaram a ter direito ao voto e reincluídas pessoas que ficaram de fora das listas eleitorais.

articles.title: Cobertura vacinal em Passos é a menor entre grandes cidades do Sul de Minas | G1
articles.standfirst: Levantamento aponta cobertura média de 74,78% nos principais imunizantes do calendário de rotina; queda na aplicação dos reforços da poliomielite acende alerta.
articles.summary: A cobertura vacinal em Passos é de 74,78%, com alerta para a baixa adesão ao reforço contra poliomielite em comparação a outras cidades do Sul de Minas.
articles.body:
Passos (MG) registrou a menor média de cobertura vacinal entre as quatro maiores cidades do Sul de Minas no conjunto dos principais imunizantes do calendário de rotina. De acordo com levantamento feito pela produção da EPTV, o município alcançou cobertura média de 74,78%.

O dado que mais preocupa é o da poliomielite. A cobertura da primeira dose é de 75,2%, mas cai para 65,2% no primeiro reforço. A diferença indica que parte das crianças inicia o esquema vacinal, mas não retorna para completar todas as doses necessárias.

A importância da imunização é levada a sério pela jornalista Maria Júlia Tomura e sua família. O filho dela, Matheu, tem apenas seis meses de vida e segue rigorosamente o calendário de vacinação. Além das vacinas oferecidas pelo Sistema Único de Saúde (SUS), os pais também investem em imunizantes disponíveis na rede particular.

"A gente se programou, se programou bastante desde a gravidez para já começar a dar prioridade para as vacinas, tanto financeiramente, que também é importante. Então a gente faz o acompanhamento do nosso neném, o Matheu, com as vacinas na rede pública e faz o complemento da vacinação aqui na rede particular também", afirmou a jornalista.

Passos registra menor média de cobertura vacinal entre as maiores cidades do Sul de Minas — Foto: Reprodução EPTV

Maria Júlia também destacou a responsabilidade coletiva envolvida na vacinação infantil.

"Não atinge somente o filho da pessoa que escolhe, porque são doenças contagiosas. Então, se você escolhe e não dá no seu filho, você pode estar prejudicando o filho de alguém também", disse.

Outras vacinas também apresentam índices abaixo da meta em Passos. Na tríplice viral, que protege contra sarampo, caxumba e rubéola, a primeira dose atinge 85,8%, enquanto a segunda fica em 75,1%. Já a vacina contra a febre amarela tem cobertura de 73,68% na primeira dose, mas apenas 74,8% desse público retorna para receber o reforço.

Em contrapartida, algumas vacinas aplicadas nos primeiros meses de vida registram melhores resultados no município. A cobertura da BCG é de 96,4%, enquanto a da vacina contra hepatite B, considerando a aplicação até 30 dias após o nascimento, chega a 95,6%.

Segundo a referência técnica de imunização, Priscila Faria, o município tem buscado facilitar o acesso às vacinas.

"As mães hoje trabalham, a carga horária de trabalho é longa, então a gente procura ter salas de vacinas abertas nos finais de semana, também em horário de almoço para facilitar. Todas as vacinas são importantes, a poliomielite é uma vacina importantíssima, ela previne contra paralisia infantil, uma doença tão grave. Então as mães devem fazer um esforço para manter o cartão em dia das crianças", afirmou.

O cenário é diferente nas demais maiores cidades da região. Em Varginha, vacinas como BCG, hepatite B, poliomielite e tríplice viral registram cobertura média superior a 100%. Em Pouso Alegre, a média de cobertura vacinal é de 96,30%. Já em Poços de Caldas, o índice é de pouco mais de 82%.

Para o pediatra André Luiz Silva, a baixa adesão aos reforços representa um risco importante para a saúde pública, já que doenças consideradas controladas podem voltar a circular.

"É uma preocupação contínua nossa. Essas doenças tão prevalentes, a vacina nós dizemos que paga um preço caro pela sua alta eficácia. Porque dá a falsa sensação de que a população, quando você não enxerga uma doença, a população está protegida. Mas se tiver índices de cobertura vacinal baixos, aí o risco de surtos e doenças graves aumenta", alertou o médico.

articles.title: Eleições SJC: Justiça Eleitoral prepara 1,5 mil urnas para domingo | G1
articles.standfirst: Equipamentos são organizados em escolas da cidade, com cuidados para garantir o sigilo do voto e a acessibilidade dos eleitores.
articles.summary: A Justiça Eleitoral prepara 1,5 mil urnas para as eleições em São José dos Campos, com foco na acessibilidade e no sigilo do voto para este domingo.
articles.body:
A Justiça Eleitoral prepara, neste sábado (3), 1.564 urnas eletrônicas que serão utilizadas nas quatro zonas eleitorais de São José dos Campos , no interior de São Paulo, durante o primeiro turno das eleições, neste domingo (4).

Servidores da Justiça Eleitoral e voluntários trabalham na montagem dos locais de votação. Entre as atividades está a instalação das cabinas eleitorais, que precisam ser posicionadas de forma a garantir o sigilo do voto.

Segundo Sarah Garcia, técnica judiciária, as urnas não podem ficar próximas a janelas, espelhos ou câmeras.

“Hoje, os servidores da Justiça Eleitoral e alguns voluntários estão preparando as sessões eleitorais nas escolas. Então está sendo feita toda a montagem das cabinas eleitorais, de forma a garantir o sigilo do voto, então a urna não pode estar perto de janelas, espelhos, câmeras.”

Urnas eletrônicas utilizadas na 127ª Zona Eleitoral, de São José dos Campos. — Foto: Reprodução/TV Vanguarda

Também é feita a organização dos cabos dos equipamentos para facilitar a circulação dos eleitores, especialmente idosos, pessoas com deficiência e com mobilidade reduzida.

“Também estamos tomando cuidado com os cabos das urnas para que seja preservada a mobilidade das pessoas, das pessoas idosas com deficiência, com mobilidade reduzida.”

Além da montagem das urnas, a equipe confere os materiais que serão utilizados durante a votação, como cartazes, cadernos de votação e listas de candidatos.

“A checagem dos materiais como um todo, os cartazes, os cadernos de votação, a lista de candidatos. Então, tudo isso está sendo feito para que amanhã o pleno exercício da democracia seja garantido a todos os cidadãos.”

articles.title: Vídeo mostra gado chegando para assistir disputa entre onças-pintadas | G1
articles.standfirst: Rebanho se aproxima de quatro felinos após dois machos iniciarem confronto em uma fazenda de Miranda, no Pantanal de Mato Grosso do Sul.
articles.summary: Rebanho se aproxima de quatro felinos após dois machos iniciarem confronto em uma fazenda de Miranda, no Pantanal de Mato Grosso do Sul.
articles.body:
Um novo vídeo publicado em uma rede social pelo técnico em agropecuária Adriel Abreu mostra o momento exato em que um rebanho de gado se aproxima de quatro onças-pintadas , logo após dois machos iniciarem uma disputa por território, na região de Miranda , no Pantanal de Mato Grosso do Sul. Veja o vídeo acima.

Nas imagens, o rebanho leva cerca de 15 segundos para chegar perto das onças, depois que os felinos se levantam e se preparam para o confronto.

A cena mostra a proximidade entre os felinos e os bois. Enquanto os dois machos brigam, outras duas onças permanecem na mesma área.

Após o confronto, um dos machos deixa o local de cabeça baixa.

"Aquele [onça] que perdeu teve que sair de cabeça baixa. O Pantanal registra essas cenas, no meio de uma invernada cheia de gado", explicou Adriel Abreu.

🔎 No jargão da pecuária, comum no Pantanal, a invernada é uma grande área de pasto cercada, destinada ao pastoreio, engorda ou descanso do gado. O termo é como se fosse um sinônimo de pastagem, onde os animais ficam soltos para se alimentar.

O vídeo foi feito na Fazenda Caiman, uma das bases de atuação do Onçafari, projeto que desenvolve pesquisas e ações de conservação e ecoturismo na região pantaneira.

Onças brigam enquanto gado 'assiste'. — Foto: Adriel Abreu

As onças-pintadas são animais territoriais e usam diferentes métodos para demarcar o espaço que ocupam. Entre os sinais deixados por elas estão fezes, urina, marcas das patas no chão, arranhões em troncos e o odor corporal liberado quando se esfregam em árvores, arbustos e rochas.

A comunicação entre os animais também ocorre por meio de sons. Um dos mais conhecidos é o esturro, vocalização semelhante a um rugido, que pode ser emitida em diferentes tons para afastar competidores, chamar filhotes ou atrair parceiros. Segundo o Onçafari, esses sons trazem informações importantes para a interação entre os felinos.

No Pantanal, os machos costumam ocupar territórios maiores do que as fêmeas. O tamanho dessas áreas varia conforme a disponibilidade de água e alimento e a quantidade de outros felinos na região.

A onça-pintada caça na terra, na água e em árvores. O animal tem uma das mordidas mais fortes entre os grandes felinos e consegue perfurar crânios e carapaças.

A conservação do Pantanal favorece a presença da espécie. A região concentra populações importantes de onças-pintadas, e a Fazenda Caiman é uma das áreas de atuação do Onçafari desde 2011.

Rebanho de gado apareceu no local segundos após as onças iniciarem a disputa. — Foto: Adriel Abreu

articles.title: Boca de lobo explode e deixa 3 pessoas feridas na Avenida Paulista, em SP | G1
articles.standfirst: Segundo a Polícia Militar, duas mulheres e um homem sofreram queimaduras e foram socorridos conscientes para a Santa Casa.
articles.summary: Segundo a Polícia Militar, duas mulheres e um homem sofreram queimaduras e foram socorridos conscientes para a Santa Casa.
articles.body:
Corpo de Bombeiros é acionado para Avenida Paulista após explosão de bueiro. — Foto: Reprodução/Redes sociais

Uma explosão em uma galeria subterrânea na Avenida Paulista, na altura do número 52, na Bela Vista, região central de São Paulo, deixou três pessoas feridas na manhã deste sábado (3).

Segundo o Corpo de Bombeiros, duas mulheres e um homem sofreram queimaduras de primeiro e segundo grau e foram socorridos conscientes para a Santa Casa de Misericórdia de São Paulo.

Os bombeiros foram acionados por volta das 11h23. Segundo informações iniciais, uma boca de lobo explodiu e atingiu as três vítimas. Três viaturas foram enviadas para atender à ocorrência.

A PM também informou que a ocorrência não tem relação com o ato político que reúne o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) e o candidato Fernando Haddad (PT) na região. A explosão ocorreu em um ponto distante da concentração de manifestantes.

articles.title: Sem citar Flávio, Lula diz que enfrenta ‘chefe de quadrilha’ e associa adversários ao crime organizado | G1
articles.standfirst: Presidente também afirmou que a eleição opõe 'democracia e soberania' a 'barbárie e corrupção' e pediu que apoiadores busquem votos até este domingo (4).
articles.summary: Presidente também afirmou que a eleição opõe 'democracia e soberania' a 'barbárie e corrupção' e pediu que apoiadores busquem votos até este domingo (4).
articles.body:
O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) afirmou neste sábado (3), durante um ato de campanha em São Paulo , que seu grupo político está enfrentando um “chefe de quadrilha” e o crime organizado.

Na fala, contudo, Lula não citou nominalmente o adversário político Flávio Bolsonaro (PL).

"Vamos às urnas amanhã [domingo] com muita tranquilidade sabendo o que está em jogo. De um lado a democracia e a soberania, do outro lado a barbárie e a corrupção. Do outro lado nós estamos trabalhando com um chefe de quadrilha. Estamos trabalhando contra crime organizado. Por isso, nós vamos precisar da força de vocês", afirmou.

A declaração foi feita na véspera do primeiro turno das eleições, no último dia da campanha nas ruas. O presidente pediu aos apoiadores que buscassem votos até a eleição deste domingo (4).

Último ato de Lula e Haddad é na Rua Augusta, no Centro de São Paulo. — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

“A partir dessa passeata ninguém descansa. É preciso conversar com as pessoas na rua, no bar, na igreja, no comércio para que a gente convença todo mundo a ir votar”, afirmou.

Em outro momento, Lula associou o governo do ex-presidente Jair Bolsonaro a irregularidades na Previdência e mencionou o banqueiro Daniel Vorcaro.

“Essa é a caminhada que prendeu a quadrilha da Previdência Social criada pelo Bolsonaro, que tornou o banqueiro prisioneiro, o [Daniel] Vorcaro. E eles estão com muito medo porque a cada dia aparece coisa nova”, declarou.

A disputa sobre o caso do INSS passou a integrar não só a campanha presidencial como também a campanha de Flávio Bolsonaro.

O adversário de Lula usou do caso como pano de fundo para associar o petista e o filho dele, Fábio Luís Lula da Silva, o Lulinha, ao escândalo. A defesa de Lulinha negou relação com as irregularidades.

Vorcaro, por sua vez, também apareceu nas investigações da CPMI. O relatório do relator pedia seu indiciamento, assim como o relatório alternativo apresentado por governistas.

O banqueiro já havia se reunido com Lula no Palácio do Planalto, em dezembro de 2024.

Em fevereiro deste ano, o presidente confirmou que recebeu Vorcaro e afirmou que havia dito ao empresário que não haveria “posição política pró ou contra o Banco Master”, mas uma investigação técnica do Banco Central.

O encontro não constou da agenda oficial do presidente.

‘De um lado está a democracia, do outro, a barbárie’

No discurso deste sábado, Lula repetiu a estratégia de apresentar a eleição como uma disputa entre dois campos políticos antagônicos.

“De um lado está a democracia, aqueles que defendem os direitos humanos, educação, ciência e tecnologia, cidadania, e do outro lado está a barbárie”, disse.

O presidente afirmou ainda que, em um eventual novo mandato, pretende promover uma “revolução educacional e tecnológica” no país.

Ao falar sobre a reta final da eleição, Lula fez um apelo a eleitores mais velhos e citou a própria idade.

“Precisamos convencer as pessoas de 70 anos que eles precisam votar pelos seus filhos, seus netos e seus bisnetos. Ninguém pode se considerar incapaz com 70 anos. Eu tenho 80 e me sinto um menino de 15”, declarou.

O presidente também disse que espera vencer a eleição no primeiro turno e convocou apoiadores a ocupar a Avenida Paulista após a votação.

Limite na distribuição de cartão de crédito

Durante o comício, o presidente Lula voltou a defender que bancos sejam proibidos de enviar cartões de crédito para as pessoas sem solicitação prévia.

Nesta quinta (1º), na reta final da corrida eleitoral, o petista disse pela primeira vez que estava discutindo com o Banco Central de proibir que os bancos dessem mais de um cartão de crédito para as pessoas.

A declaração repercutiu entre a oposição. Na sexta-feira (2), Lula se posicionou nas redes sociais afirmando que os adversários defendem "bilionários donos de operadoras de cartões.

"Claro que sei da importância do crédito para a vida das famílias. Cada cidadão tem o direito de ter quantos cartões de crédito quiser", escreveu o presidente na ocasião.

"O que não aceito é que bancos enviem para a casa das pessoas sem que elas tenham solicitado. Vamos acabar com essa prática e com os juros abusivos no Brasil."

Neste sábado, Lula afirmou que "mentirosos tentaram mentir" a seu respeito.

"O que eu acho é que o cartão de crédito tem que ser distribuído com seriedade para quem pedir cartão de crédito. Quem quiser cartão de crédito que peça para o banco. O banco não pode ficar mandando para a casa das pessoas sem as pessoas pedirem", disse o petista em São Paulo.

"Cartão de crédito é responsabilidade. Primeiro porque o juros do cartão de crédito é uma roubalheira. Por isso, no quarto mandato vamos moralizar essa coisa do crédito Brasil. O sistema financeiro quer ganhar dinheiro, ganhe dinheiro investindo na produção e não extorquindo o povo brasileiro com taxa de juros impagáveis."

articles.title: De muletas, morador de Volta Redonda encara 150 km a pé até Aparecida | G1
articles.standfirst: Após enfrentar grave acidente de moto em 2010 e amputar a perna em 2024, Rafael Teixeira encara o desafio da vida rumo ao Santuário Nacional de Aparecida, no Vale do Paraíba, em São Paulo.
articles.summary: Após enfrentar grave acidente de moto em 2010 e amputar a perna em 2024, Rafael Teixeira encara o desafio da vida rumo ao Santuário Nacional de Aparecida, no Vale do Paraíba (SP).
articles.body:
De muletas e sem apoio, morador de Volta Redonda encara 150 km a pé até Aparecida — Foto: Divulgação/Rafael Teixeira

O morador do bairro Volta Grande 1, em Volta Redonda (RJ), Rafael Teixeira, deu início ao que considera um dos maiores testes de resistência da própria vida. Ele pretende percorrer a pé, apoiado apenas em um par de muletas e sem carro de escolta ou equipe de apoio, cerca de 150 quilômetros até o Santuário Nacional de Aparecida, no Vale do Paraíba paulista. A largada da romaria solitária aconteceu na última quarta-feira (30).

Com mais de 14 mil seguidores nas redes sociais, onde compartilha a rotina de treinos e mensagens motivacionais, o atleta planeja concluir o trajeto em 10 dias, mantendo uma média de 15 quilômetros a cada jornada pelas margens da Via Dutra.

A virada radical na rotina de Rafael ocorreu na noite de 10 de março de 2010. À época, ele conciliava a graduação em Direito em uma universidade privada e o trabalho na Procuradoria Municipal de Barra Mansa. Por volta das 22h, quando voltava para casa pilotando uma moto, foi vítima de um grave acidente de trânsito na altura do bairro Ponte Alta.

"Eu até digo: do terno e gravata eu fui para as fraldas em questão de segundos", recorda Rafael.

O episódio deu início a uma trajetória de tratamento de 15 anos. Na tentativa de evitar a perda da perna esquerda, ele foi submetido a 27 procedimentos cirúrgicos e enfrentou meses seguidos acamado. O quadro clínico, contudo, evoluiu com três diagnósticos graves de osteomielite, que é uma infecção bacteriana que atinge a estrutura óssea. A amputação acabou se tornando inevitável e foi realizada na véspera do Natal de 2024.

"Fiquei 27 períodos acamado, usei fraldas, e ficava olhando para o teto branco e conversando com Deus pedindo para recuperar minha autonomia e liberdade de andar sem depender dos outros", contou.

Rafael foi submetido a 27 procedimentos cirúrgicos e enfrentou meses seguidos acamado. — Foto: Divulgação/Rafael Teixeira

A reabilitação ganhou novo fôlego com a prática esportiva. Rafael chegou a se mudar para São Paulo para treinar modalidades paralímpicas, como vôlei sentado e halterofilismo, mas retornou à região devido aos custos de permanência na capital paulista. Em Volta Redonda, adaptou-se às corridas de rua com muletas.

Ele encontrou uma forma que encontrou para se manter integrado à comunidade esportiva. A evolução rápida rendeu a conclusão dos 21 quilômetros da Meia Maratona do Rio em 2025, apenas um ano após a cirurgia.

Rafael fez 21 km da Meia Maratona do Rio em 2025, um ano após cirurgia. — Foto: Divulgação/Rafael Teixeira

Agora, o desafio até Aparecida simboliza a consolidação desse processo de retomada. Sozinho, o atleta encara a jornada como um retiro para celebrar a independência reconquistada e levar esperança a quem também atravessa momentos difíceis.

"Além de cada passo de muletas nessa romaria ser um sacrifício pessoal e retiro espiritual de agradecimento a Deus e Nossa Senhora Aparecida, espero que através da divulgação ajude pessoas que estão enfrentando problemas com a própria saúde mental. A missão de Deus na minha vida também é impactar os outros, inspirar, gerar transformação de atitude", conclui.

articles.summary: Em sua 34ª edição, celebração terá romarias, procissões e missas e reunirá fiéis no Cohatrac e em outros pontos da capital.
articles.body:
Em sua 34ª edição, celebração terá romarias, procissões e missas e reunirá fiéis no Cohatrac e em outros pontos da capital. — Foto: Divulgação

O Círio de Nazaré, realizado pelo Santuário Nossa Senhora de Nazaré, no bairro Cohatrac, em São Luís, será celebrado de 8 a 18 de outubro. Em sua 34ª edição, a programação reúne missas, peregrinações, romarias e procissões e deve atrair fiéis de diferentes regiões do Maranhão.

Neste ano, o Círio tem como tema “Santuário de Luz” e lema “Recebei o Espírito Santo” (Jo 20,22). Embora a programação principal aconteça em outubro, as atividades começaram em setembro e se estendem por cerca de 50 dias.

Entre os principais momentos estão o Círio das Crianças, a Romaria a Pé, a Romaria Marítima e as procissões de encerramento.

O Círio das Crianças será realizado de 2 a 4 de outubro, com missas todos os dias, às 18h, além de uma apresentação cultural do grupo Vozes de Nazaré.

No dia 10 de outubro, será realizada a Romaria a Pé. A concentração será na Igreja do Carmo, no Centro de São Luís, com saída prevista para as 23h.

Já no dia 12 de outubro, ocorre a Romaria Marítima. A concentração será na região da Praia Grande, no Centro, às 7h.

No dia 17 de outubro, será realizada a Procissão da Luz e o translado da imagem. A programação começa às 17h, com uma missa na Praça Nossa Senhora de Nazaré, em frente ao Santuário, no Cohatrac.

Após a celebração, os fiéis seguirão em procissão luminosa até a Igreja Nossa Senhora do Perpétuo Socorro, na Cohab.

O encerramento do Círio acontece no dia 18 de outubro. A concentração será às 16h30, na Igreja Nossa Senhora do Perpétuo Socorro. A procissão terá início às 17h, com destino ao Santuário de Nazaré, no Cohatrac.

No local, será celebrada a missa de encerramento, presidida pelo arcebispo de São Luís, Dom Gilberto Pastana.

2 a 4 de outubro: Círio das Crianças, com missas às 18h e apresentação cultural.

10 de outubro: Romaria a Pé, com concentração na Igreja do Carmo e saída às 23h.

12 de outubro: Romaria Marítima, com concentração na região da Praia Grande, às 7h.

17 de outubro: Procissão da Luz e translado da imagem, a partir das 17h.

18 de outubro: Procissão de encerramento, às 17h, seguida de missa no Santuário de Nazaré.

Preparação envolve cerca de 800 voluntários

A preparação para o Círio começa antes da programação principal. Em setembro, são realizadas peregrinações com encontros em famílias, instituições, hospitais, escolas e outros municípios maranhenses.

Também são realizadas missas em ruas e praças do Cohatrac. Ao longo dos cerca de 50 dias de programação, os fiéis participam ainda de celebrações eucarísticas, confissões e adorações ao Santíssimo Sacramento.

“É um verdadeiro retiro espiritual, que acontece aqui no Cohatrac”, afirmou a paroquiana Bernadete Pacheco, que acompanha as peregrinações nas famílias.

Segundo a organização, cerca de 800 leigos e leigas participam voluntariamente da preparação e realização do Círio. Eles estão distribuídos em 17 equipes de serviço, entre elas Comissão do Círio, Apoio, Liturgia, Decoração, Peregrinação, Guarda, Comunicação, Largo e Comissão do Círio das Crianças.

Além da dimensão religiosa, o Círio de Nazaré também é reconhecido como manifestação cultural. Desde 2019, a celebração é considerada Patrimônio Cultural e Imaterial do Estado do Maranhão, por meio da Lei nº 11.127/2019.

Em 2024, o Círio também foi reconhecido por lei federal como Manifestação da Cultura Nacional.

A programação inclui ainda iniciativas voltadas para outras áreas, como o Círio Solidário, Círio Ecológico, Círio Esportivo e Círio Cultural.

Segundo a organização, o lançamento do Círio ocorreu em 28 de junho, data do aniversário de fundação da paróquia. A partir da data, voluntários passaram a atuar na preparação das atividades que integram a programação deste ano

articles.title: 'No evidence of fracture': Bengal govt to probe Mamata Banerjee's 2021 'injury'
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari on Saturday accused his predecessor Mamata Banerjee of faking her injury during the 2021 state
articles.body: NEW DELHI: West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari on Saturday accused his predecessor Mamata Banerjee of faking her injury during the 2021 state assembly elections.Adhikari added that a fresh inquiry would be launched to probe Mamata Banerjee's “false claims” of injury. He claimed that there was no evidence of fracture or dislocation in the-then CM's medical report issued by treating hospital.“Mamata Banerjee faked her leg injury during campaigning in Nandigram in 2021. We have the medical report which stated that there was no evidence of fracture or dislocation. We will initiate an investigation into the matter,” PTI quoted Adhikari as saying at a press conference in Kolkata. He also displayed the TMC supremo’s medical report issued by the Bangur Institute of Neuroscience.“Her false allegation insulted the people of Nandigram. I will come out with more details after the MCC (model code of conduct) is lifted after October 9... Today, I am saying this in support of my claims made yesterday,” he added.His remarks came ahead of the Nandigram byelection scheduled for October 6. The counting of votes will be held on October 9.The Nandigram constituency was vacated by Adhikari after he defeated Mamata Banerjee in her Bhabanipore stronghold in the West Bengal assembly elections in April. He also won from Nandigram, his traditional seat, but chose to keep Bhabanipore.On March 10, 2021, Mamata Banerjee, the-then chief minister, sustained injuries to her left leg and waist while campaigning in the Reyapara area of Birulia in Nandigram.She initially alleged that a few unidentified people had deliberately pushed her against the door of her open car, causing it to slam into her left leg amid a heavy crowd.In a video message from the hospital, she said the “massive crowd” had pressed against her car while she was greeting supporters, causing her leg to be crushed and injured.The TMC supremo was diagnosed with severe bone and ligament injuries to her left ankle and foot, along with bruising and pain in her right shoulder, forearm, neck and waist. She was subsequently taken to Kolkata and admitted to the state-run SSKM Hospital.Mamata Banerjee was discharged two days later, on March 12, with her left foot in a cast. She subsequently resumed campaigning in a wheelchair.The TMC won 213 of the 294 seats in the 2021 assembly elections, while the BJP secured 77.However, the BJP won the 2026 assembly elections, securing 207 seats and forming its first government in West Bengal, while the TMC won 80 seats and was voted out of power after 15 years.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: BROADCAST BIAS: From FlyDubai to Benghazi, the media struggle to keep politics out of terrorism
articles.summary: FlyDubai cockpit violence coverage drew criticism as networks worried Trump and Netanyahu might spin the terrorism incident for political gain.
articles.body: When news of a potential terrorist attack breaks, the first draft can sound like an attempt to maintain political correctness. The New York Times came under attack on Wednesday for tweeting, "A plane flying from Dubai to Israel was diverted after an altercation between the pilot and co-pilot, Israeli officials said." After people mocked the "altercation" lingo, the Times PR team counter-attacked: "Our headlines and live coverage contain all the facts we're able to confirm as we confirm them. Unlike activists and partisans, we don't publish speculation or unverified information." Anyone who thinks The Times doesn’t give off partisan activist vibes isn’t reading it. NEW YORK TIMES ISSUES CORRECTION, DELETES LINE QUESTIONING IF ISRAELIS WERE VICTIMS OF OCT 7 TERROR ATTACK The British Broadcasting Corporation posted a similarly bland breaking-news headline: "Israel-bound flight diverted after fight between pilots." This sounded a little like a verbal spat. At least the brief report underneath relayed, "Two Israeli officials said the co-pilot is believed to have stabbed the captain and tried to crash the plane." The American broadcast networks didn’t perform this way on Wednesday morning. On "Today," NBC reporter Matt Bradley was more straightforward: "There was some sort of violent incident on board that flight. The plane sent out a hijacking alert." A passenger on the plane correctly relayed the pilot had been stabbed. FLYDUBAI PILOT SHOWED WORLD 'THE HIGHEST FORM OF COURAGE,' INDIA'S PM SAYS ABC’s Ian Pannell used the T-word: "This is a rapidly developing story, but it is looking increasingly like a terrorist incident." But the usual instinct for elitist media is to move very slowly to guess about the motive – even if it might seem obvious. An attempted hijacking of a plane full of Israelis headed for Tel Aviv suggests a hostility to Israel. The Israelis clearly suspected a new version of the 9/11 hijacking, as the networks reported they scrambled jets to intercept the Boeing 737 Max before standing down. HERO FLYDUBAI PILOT SAYS HE WAS 'FIGHTING FOR MY LIFE' AS PLANE PLUNGED AFTER COPILOT ATTACK But some networks had to smell politics in their hunt for a motive. "PBS News Hour" anchor Geoff Bennett talked to former Clinton and Obama official Juliette Kayyem. He began: "Israel's prime minister says the co-pilot underwent what he called Islamist radical indoctrination. President [Donald] Trump has pointed to Iran. Neither has provided evidence. … What can we responsibly say, if anything, about the motive at this point?" Kayyem replied: "Right. So, and I'm glad you say that about responsibly say. After every crisis, terror incident, disaster, there's a narrative that forms very early that is often pushed for political reasons. I think we should just put those to the side aside right now, that that just happens. There are elections." CBC TELLS JOURNALISTS NOT TO CALL 9/11 ‘TERRORIST ATTACKS’ IN INTERNAL GUIDANCE Then Kayyem acknowledged that it seems obvious that the "leading theory" would be a co-pilot trying to crash a plane of Israelis in Israel suggests terrorism. "What we don't know and the suspicion or allegations that this is related to a terrorist organization or even Iran is what that radicalization process was like." It could be self-radicalization, or "If it's state-sponsored terrorism, like Iran, a country that Israel and the United States have started a war against, that is a very different consequence." But she suggested it could just be "mental-health" issues. An expert on CNN suggested it might just be "workplace violence." Well, the cockpit is a workplace, but the desperation here is obvious. NPR’s "Morning Edition" turned to Democrat-leaning former CNN analyst Philip Mudd, asking him if the political motivations of Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin "Bibi" Netanyahu are going to cloud the investigation. The British Broadcasting Corporation posted a similarly bland breaking-news headline: "Israel-bound flight diverted after fight between pilots." This sounded a little like a verbal spat. Terrorism incidents during election season might remind Americans of Sept. 11, 2012 – when a pack of terrorists broke into the American consulate in Benghazi, Libya, leading to the death of the U.S. ambassador and three other Americans. All the networks turned on Republican nominee Mitt Romney for questioning President Barack Obama’s handling of Libya. A Media Research Center analysis of the first night of Benghazi coverage found the Romney-is-rude angle received nine minutes and 28 seconds of coverage on ABC, CBS, and NBC, while only 25 seconds focused on Obama’s Middle East policies. Obama turned to CBS reporter Steve Kroft, his reliable "60 Minutes" softball pitcher, and said, "Governor Romney seems to have a tendency to shoot first and aim later" when you have to "make sure that the statements you make are backed up by the facts." Kroft nudged: "Do you think it was irresponsible?" Obama said, "I’ll let the American people judge that." Sure, after the networks pounded home the Romney attacks. CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION A few days later, Team Obama bizarrely claimed the Benghazi attack could be blamed on a YouTube video that spurred spontaneous protests, so there was no "pre-planned attack." Right before the election, CBS posted more of Kroft’s Obama interview in September where Obama said it was an attack on Americans, not a protest. But that didn’t air on television until the election was over. articles.title: California tech company owner arrested over alleged $300 million China chip-smuggling scheme
articles.summary: A California technology company owner has been arrested on charges of allegedly smuggling more than USD 300 million in export-controlled computer servers
articles.body: A California technology company owner has been arrested on charges of allegedly smuggling more than USD 300 million in export-controlled computer servers containing US-made graphics processing units (GPUs) to China, according to federal prosecutors.The US Department of Justice said Greg Lui, 38, also known as Yiu Kong Lui, was arrested after being charged in a three-count federal indictment. Lui, who owns City of Industry-based Earthmade Computer Inc., allegedly used third countries, false paperwork and freight-forwarding arrangements to send restricted technology to China without the required US export licences.According to the indictment, the alleged scheme operated between 2023 and 2024. Lui and his co-conspirators allegedly bought export-controlled servers through Earthmade and routed them to countries including Malaysia and Singapore, where the required US export licence was not needed, before arranging for the equipment to be re-exported to China.Prosecutors allege the servers contained high-end GPUs used for Super Intelligence (SI) computing. Lui allegedly knew that the actual end users were in China while providing US manufacturers with documents showing permitted destinations and end users.The indictment alleges that Lui and his associates used freight-forwarding companies to move the servers from the US to third countries before they were sent on to China. From January to October 2024, Earthmade allegedly received more than $176 million from two Malaysia-based shipment companies.In one instance cited by prosecutors, Lui placed an order in January 2024 for 27 servers worth about $7.6 million. The servers were shipped from Los Angeles to Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia. A subsequent email to a Malaysian government official allegedly indicated that the 27 servers had been transshipped to a China-based buyer.Lui faces charges of conspiracy to violate the Export Control Reform Act and Export Administration Regulations, outbound smuggling and conspiracy to commit money laundering.If convicted, he could face a maximum sentence of 20 years on the export-control conspiracy charge, 20 years on the money-laundering conspiracy charge and 10 years on the smuggling charge.The FBI, the Defence Criminal Investigative Service and the Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security Office of Export Enforcement are investigating the case.The DOJ said the indictment contains allegations only, and Lui is presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in court.You use AI every day. articles.title: A Florida sea captain spent 3 years searching for a Scottish castle; he bought one built after a family feud and said to be haunted
articles.summary: A Florida sea captain has bought one of Scotland's unusual castles after a three-year search for the right property.
articles.body: A Florida sea captain has bought one of Scotland's unusual castles after a three-year search for the right property. Lance Holmquist and his wife, Suzanne, purchased Carbisdale Castle in Sutherland for just under £3.9 million, describing their first visit to the Highland landmark as love at first sight, according to the BBC. The castle is known as the “Castle of Spite” because of the family dispute surrounding its construction, and it is also said to be haunted by a ghost called Betty. Lance has spent 44 years in the maritime industry, including more than 30 as a captain based in Key Largo, Florida, while Suzanne, who was born in London and grew up in Glasgow, runs a boat charter business with him and previously worked as a TV editor before moving to the United States about 25 years ago.How Lance and Suzanne Holmquist found Carbisdale Castle after 3 years searching Ireland and ScotlandThe couple had been looking to buy a castle in Ireland or Scotland for about three years before discovering Carbisdale. Suzanne said Lance loved the countryside in Ireland, so she suggested he visit the Scottish Highlands as well. They looked at several properties but repeatedly found they were too late to act on places they liked. Then they saw Carbisdale. Suzanne said they fell in love with the castle on their first day there, after they returned for a viewing a few months after discovering it. Lance, a self-confessed fan of castles and old pirate stories, had long wanted to own one. The couple plan to begin by offering the castle for short-term stays before developing it into a boutique hotel. Law firm Thorntons' Inverness team advised on the acquisition, while their friend David Walton became a 10% investment partner.The Castle of Spite: how a family feud shaped Carbisdale Castle and its 3-faced clock towerCarbisdale Castle was built in the early 20th century for Mary Caroline, the Dowager Duchess of Sutherland, following a dispute over her late husband's estate. The Highland Historic Environment Record dates the building to 1907. The settlement following the dispute allowed the Duchess to have a residence built outside the Sutherland family's estate. Carbisdale was constructed on a hillside in a position from which it could be seen from Sutherland. The location later became associated with the nickname “Castle of Spite”, reflecting the long-standing story that the Duchess chose the site to spite her husband's family. The castle's clock tower has clock faces on three sides, with the side facing Sutherland left blank. It has traditionally been said that this was a snub to her former in-laws, with the blank side linked to the story that she did not want to give them the time of day. That explanation is part of the castle's long-running folklore rather than a documented statement of the Duchess's motive. Carbisdale is a Category B-listed building. It later passed to the Norwegian Salvesen family and was used as a refuge for members of the Norwegian royal family during the Second World War. In 1945, it was given to the Scottish Youth Hostels Association and operated as a youth hostel until 2011, when it closed amid the need for repairs.What comes next for Carbisdale Castle, from short-term lets to a boutique hotelThe Holmquists plan to begin by offering the castle for short-term stays before developing it into a boutique hotel. The couple have said they want the venture to preserve the history of the property and its surroundings. Suzanne said each of the castle's windows has its own story. The couple have also received messages of welcome from the local community, while Lance plans to continue running his charter business in Florida. Lance joked that after decades of Florida sunshine, Scottish weather could mean finally wearing a jumper. He also said he was looking forward to seeing his first deer in the Highlands and joked that his love of boats could lead him to take a small rowing boat onto a nearby loch. In Florida, he is used to encounters with manatees, which are also known as sea cows.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.
