articles.title: In 1916, the US began releasing Asian lady beetles to control aphids and scale insects; decades later Harmonia axyridis became invasive and was linked to declines of native ladybirds
articles.summary: The multicoloured Asian lady beetle was introduced to the United States with a clear purpose.
articles.body: The multicoloured Asian lady beetle was introduced to the United States with a clear purpose. Starting as early as 1916, agricultural officials released the insect, scientifically known as Harmonia axyridis, in an effort to control aphids, scale insects and other crop pests without relying as heavily on chemical insecticides. It was an appealing form of biological control, but the story took an unexpected turn. After the species established wild populations in the late 1980s, it spread rapidly across the country and beyond, becoming one of the world’s most successful invasive insects. According to reports by the USDA Agricultural Research Service, it can outcompete native ladybirds and is now regarded as an invasive species in many regions.An import meant to help farmersThe multicoloured Asian lady beetle is native to Asia, where it feeds on aphids and other soft-bodied arthropods. Those feeding habits made it attractive to US agricultural researchers looking for natural ways to control pests in orchards, forests, gardens and field crops. Aphids can damage plants by extracting sap, while scale insects can weaken trees and shrubs, so a predator that consumed large numbers of these pests appeared to be a useful ally.Federal, state and private entomologists released Harmonia axyridis at several locations over the years. The beetles were meant to reduce pest populations and, in turn, lower the need for insecticides. In some settings, that promise was fulfilled, especially in pecan orchards and on ornamental plants, where the beetles helped control aphids.At the time, biological control was widely viewed as a practical alternative to chemical pest management. Introducing predators can offer benefits when the predator remains focused on its target prey and fits into the new ecosystem without causing disruption. The challenge is that ecosystems are complex, and an insect that is helpful in one place can behave very differently after crossing continents.The first wild populationsAlthough releases began as early as 1916, the first established US populations of multicoloured Asian lady beetles were not documented until 1988. They were found in Louisiana near the busy port of New Orleans, far from many of the locations where planned releases had occurred. That gap raised a key question: did the species establish because of intentional releases, accidental introductions through trade, or both?USDA researchers note that accidental entries likely occurred through imported nursery stock at ports in Delaware and South Carolina. This makes it difficult to trace the exact origin of the invasion. What is clear is that once Harmonia axyridis gained a foothold, it spread rapidly through North America and later across other continents.The beetle’s success was helped by its adaptability. It can survive in orchards, forests, row crops, gardens and urban areas, feeding on a broad range of prey. It also reproduces quickly, with development from egg to adult taking roughly 15 to 25 days depending on temperature and food availability. These traits gave it a major advantage in new habitats, as per the reports.A familiar beetle with many facesThe Asian lady beetle can be difficult to identify because its appearance varies greatly. Its wing covers may range from black to mustard yellow or red, and the number of spots can vary from none to many. In the United States, a common form is mustard to red with 16 or more black spots, but the diversity in colour and markings means it is not always easy to distinguish from native species at a glance.Like other ladybirds, it goes through four distinct life stages: egg, larva, pupa and adult. Females begin laying eggs on host plants in early spring, and the larvae immediately begin hunting aphids and other soft-bodied prey after hatching. Both adults and larvae are active predators, meaning the species can have a strong effect on insect populations wherever it becomes abundant.That feeding efficiency is exactly what made the beetle valuable to agriculture. However, a voracious appetite is not limited to crop pests. It can also put pressure on native ladybirds that depend on the same food sources, turning an agricultural helper into a conservation concern.When helpful became harmfulThe USDA describes the Asian lady beetle as a mixed blessing. It remains an effective predator of aphids and other pests, but has also become a nuisance in homes and a threat to biodiversity. In invaded countries Harmonia axyridis is considered invasive as it can outcompete other ladybug species for food and habitat.Native ladybugs might be unable to compete with a highly adaptable newcomer moving into the same ecological niche. Harmonia axyridis is larger than many native species, highly mobile and able to use a wide range of habitats. Its ability to find food across different crops and landscapes can give it an advantage when prey is scarce.The beetle also has strong defences. USDA research notes that it possesses chemical, mechanical and microbiological anti-predator traits that cause many predators to avoid it. These defences reduce the natural pressure that might otherwise limit its numbers, allowing populations to increase and spread.A difficult species to controlScientists have studied whether predators and parasitoids could naturally slow the Asian lady beetle’s expansion. The evidence suggests that many vertebrate and invertebrate predators in invaded regions are relatively ineffective at limiting the beetle. Some birds and insects can consume it, but its defensive adaptations often make it an unappealing or difficult target.Parasitoids, organisms that develop on or inside a host and ultimately kill it, may offer some potential. USDA researchers identified certain true flies in the genus Phalacrotophora as possible natural enemies capable of overcoming some of the beetle’s defences. However, researchers stress that more work is needed to understand whether these relationships can meaningfully reduce populations at a larger scale.The case of Harmonia axyridis illustrates a common pattern in biological invasions. A species introduced without its full set of predators, parasites and ecological constraints may initially flourish. Over time, native species may adapt and new relationships may form, but that process can take years or decades and may not undo the harm already caused.A nuisance in homes tooFor homeowners, the most visible problem often arrives in autumn. As temperatures drop, adult Asian lady beetles seek sheltered places to overwinter, including homes, sheds and other buildings. They are particularly drawn to light-coloured structures, such as white, grey and yellow houses, which can act as visual cues for the insects.The beetles do not damage structures in the way termites or carpenter ants do. They do not chew wood, bore through walls, feed on carpets, or lay eggs indoors. However, they can gather in large numbers in wall spaces and then enter living areas on warm winter or early spring days while searching for an exit.When disturbed or crushed, the insects can release a yellow, unpleasant-smelling fluid from their leg joints in a defensive behaviour known as reflex bleeding. The fluid can stain walls and fabrics, making the beetles unwelcome guests despite their role as pest predators. USDA guidance recommends sealing exterior cracks and crevices before autumn and using a vacuum or broom to remove beetles that enter indoor spaces.Lessons from a century-old decisionThe Asian lady beetle’s journey from a planned pest-control import to a widespread invasive species offers an important lesson about ecological caution. Biocontrol reduces pesticide use and protects crops, but all nonnative species come with risks that aren’t always immediately apparent. A predator may control one pest while competing with native species or creating new problems elsewhere.More than a century after the first US releases, Harmonia axyridis remains both useful and disruptive. It still has some use controlling aphids in certain agricultural settings, but the unintended consequences of its spread have come at a cost to native ladybugs and home comfort. Its history is a warning that even well-meaning attempts to help the environment have to be assessed not just on the benefits they bring in the short term, but on what they might lead to in the longer term.You use AI every day. articles.summary: The all-in-chief is in a tearing hurry to tear down historic edifices Donald Trump, the self-styled builder-in-chief may be in a tearing hurry to tear
articles.body: The all-in-chief is in a tearing hurry to tear down historic edificesDonald Trump, the self-styled builder-in-chief may be in a tearing hurry to tear down historic edifices to erect his own. But he draws the line at the storied Oval Office that he has so lovingly drowned in a sea of gold.The Secret Service had suggested the president’s office be “taken down,” to build a more fortified one, but he pushed back at the idea claims the man who tore down the East Wing to make way for his $400 million big beautiful ballroom.“I see the Secret Service looking, and I say, ‘What are you guys looking at?’ ‘Sir, we think the Oval Office should be taken down, and we’ll build a new one, sir,'” he told Time magazine in an interview.“I said, ‘My a–, you can’t build a new one. This is a special place.'”But Trump refused to promise not to tear down the iconic Kennedy Center for Performing Arts after a judge refused to let his handpicked board to put back his name on its facade as its restorer and renovator.“I’m not committing to anything,” Trump told Time. “We’re going to see how it plays out in court.”Trump has argued that the Kennedy Center was structurally unsafe and needed to be closed to undergo a two-year, $250 million renovation, but he won’t allow renovations to start unless he can put his name on the building.But to ensure “that nobody should be allowed to rip down this beautiful room,” after he leaves the Oval Office, Trump is mulling making it a federal landmark.During the interview, Trump also ranted about judges, showed off pictures of his White House renovations, and constantly made a litany of complaints about the ‘unfair fake’ media.And as with 56 appearances on Time’s cover, Trump surpassed Richard Nixon, who held the record for more than half a century, he posted a collage of them all crowning himself “TIME’s cover king.”Earlier, after privately huddling with 20 tech titans at a White House lunch, Trump continued to push back on calls for new safety regulations for artificial intelligence.“There’s a belief that there should be tremendous self-regulation, and we automatically have regulation with the Department of Justice, the FBI, all of that,” said Trump, flanked by tech and government leaders. Among them was Alphabet CEO Sundar Pichai, whom he playfully introduced as “a monster.”“What a great life! To be a Monster and not have to go through this. All you have to know is – sundarr! Sundar is his name,” he joked leaving Pichai to respond sheepishly, “Hopefully a better tagline than ‘I’m a monster’.”Trump also unveiled America.gov, a website that features an AI-powered tool meant to serve as a “one-stop shop” for Americans navigating government services.But to his chagrin the chatbot, which draws upon 29,000 government websites to formulate its answers, tells the truth ever ready to debunk his false claims on all sorts of things from who won the 2020 election to whether windmills drive whales “loco.”“Joseph R. Biden Jr. won the 2020 U.S. presidential election,” says the bot without hedging its bets, and “U.S. federal science agencies do not find that windmills are “driving whales insane.”Would it be next on Trump’s chopping block?Meanwhile, Trump’s secretary of offense (oops war), Pete Hegseth, who according to a new book got the job because he looked good on TV, trumpeted his own plans to slash the Pentagon.“We are no longer the woke department or the weak department. Simple translation of that: No fatties, no trannies, no beardos, no weirdos, no wimps, no radicals. Just warriors,” Hegseth said delivering what was touted as a “State of the Force” address.Then for once acknowledging he’s “done a very bad job of explaining how good the country is doing,” Trump set out on a punishing tour of 17 states for 36 events in 30 days, to energize Republican voters ahead of the crucial midterm elections.With his own record low approval ratings amid an unpopular war and rising prices, Trump no longer wants voters to just pretend he’s on the ballot, he also wants to tell them in person,“We’re worried.”During a rally in Oklahoma, he once again promised that “if the Republicans win, you will each have $5,000 in your pocket and the economic success for our country like you’ve never seen before” — a promise that critics have called a bribe.But brushing aside ethical concerns, the White House expanded a taxpayer-paid ad campaign boosting Trump. In the latest ad brought to you by Uncle Sam, Trump is seen staring into the camera as he vows to drive his political enemies from power.But a little old woman scored a victory over the world’s most powerful man with Trump finally agreeing to end his court fight against $5 million verdict in E. Jean Carroll case.As Carroll has already received the payout with interest in the 2023 sexual abuse and defamation civil trial against Trump, the decision revealed by a U.S. court of appeals puts the final seal on the case.Yet a spokesperson for Trump’s legal team again dismissed the whole affair as another ‘witch hunt’ stating, “The American People stand with President Trump as they demand an immediate end to all of the Witch Hunts, including the Democrat-funded travesty of the Carroll Hoaxes.”Back in Washington, Trump signed an executive order targeting mosquitoes in the capital. It directs the Interior Department to “develop and implement a campaign” within 60 days to reduce certain mosquito species in D.C. by 90 percent.The edict stipulates that only “common sense, non-chemical technology-enabled measures” can be used — but does not specify whether it also covers annoying pests of the media kind!(By arrangement with The American Bazaar)You use AI every day. articles.summary: LUCKNOW: A 50-year-old RSS functionary was killed following a violent assault in Bheekam Chhapra village under Lar police station limits in Deoria.
articles.body: LUCKNOW: A 50-year-old RSS functionary was killed following a violent assault in Bheekam Chhapra village under Lar police station limits in Deoria.The deceased Rameshwar Tiwari, was assaulted during a clash on Oct 1 and next day he succumbed to his injuries. Following his death, Tiwari’s wife, Amrita Devi, lodged an FIR against four named and ten unidentified persons.Four police personnel including Station officer Lar have been suspended following the incident, while senior officers are monitoring the investigation. Police said the assault was an outcome of old land property issue within the family.Those suspended are Lar SHO Rakesh Singh, beat sub-inspector Rammoorat Ram, and constables Chandrabhan Bharti and Pritam Yadav.“Four policemen have been suspended for negligence. Four police teams have been formed and are conducting raids to arrest the accused,” DIG Gorakhpur Range, S Channappa said.According to the FIR registered on the complaint of Tiwari’s wife, Amrita Devi, seven named accused and 10 unidentified persons have been booked under several provisions of the BNS sections 103(1) (murder), 191(2) and 191(3) relate to rioting, including rioting while armed with a deadly weapon; 190 (unlawful assembly), 115(2) (voluntarily causing grievous hurt), 351(3) (criminal intimidation) and others.The FIR names Sanjay Tiwari, Deepak Tiwari, Pranjal Tiwari, Abhineet Tiwari, Aditya Tiwari and Nikhil Tiwari, all residents of Bhikham Chhapra.As per FIR, around 5 pm on October 1, the accused allegedly arrived at Tiwari’s house armed with sticks, a hammer and a heavy iron tool. Amrita alleged that the group attacked her husband on the head with the hammer and iron implement over an old dispute, leaving him unconscious and seriously injured.When she attempted to intervene, she too was allegedly assaulted, the complaint states.Tiwari was taken first to the Lar Community Health Centre, from where doctors referred him to Maharshi Devraha Baba Medical College in Deoria because of his critical condition. He was declared dead on arrival at the medical college, according to the FIR.Police and local residents said the two sides had been in conflict for about a year. According to local accounts, a dispute had earlier arisen over irrigation of wheat crops. The disagreement was subsequently settled, but tensions reportedly continued.There were also discussions about a dispute over land used as a passage, with the two sides having confronted each other on earlier occasions.On Thursday, road-pitching work was underway along the main road adjoining Tiwari’s house. Tiwari reportedly had a speed breaker constructed near his residence to slow down vehicles. Members of the other side objected to the construction, following which an argument broke out.The FIR alleges that the confrontation escalated when the accused reached near Tiwari’s house and attacked him with weapons.There were also previous incidents linked to the dispute. articles.title: Coast Guard searches for missing jet carrying 6 people off Nantucket
articles.summary: A Gulfstream G-100 carrying six people lost contact with air traffic controllers early the morning of Oct. 3, authorities said.
articles.body:
The U.S. Coast Guard is searching off the coast of Nantucket for a missing jet carrying six people after it went missing the morning of Oct. 3.

The jet, a Gulfstream G-100, lost contact with flight controllers early in the morning, the Coast Guard's Northeast District said. The Federal Aviation Administration said in a statement to USA TODAY that it issued a search and rescue alert notice for the jet at about 1:20 a.m. local time.

The six people on board were flying from L.F. Wade International Airport in Bermuda to Boston Logan International Airport, the FAA said.

Authorities are searching with air and surface crews off the coast of Nantucket, the island south of Cape Cod. Bermuda is nearly 700 miles from Nantucket.

articles.title: A Cleveland factory once belonged to America’s largest gasoline-car maker and faced demolition this year; a developer has now bought the 7.3-acre, 260,000-sq-ft complex for $300,000 and plans to reuse it
articles.summary: There was a time when Cleveland’s Berea Road was home to one of America’s most important automobile factories.
articles.body: There was a time when Cleveland’s Berea Road was home to one of America’s most important automobile factories. Now, after decades of changing uses and a near-demolition, the sprawling former Winton Motor Carriage Works is getting another chance. According to NEOtrans, aGreater Cleveland developer has acquired the long-vacant industrial complex for $300,000 and is preparing a phased redevelopment of the historic property. Scroll down to read the details.From demolition target to redevelopmentAccording to NEOtrans report, the four-parcel property in Cleveland’s Cudell neighborhood covers 7.3 acres and contains about 260,000 square feet of brick factory buildings. Developer John Ellis, through Winton Works Ltd., led the acquisition from Legacy Property Investments VI Ltd., an affiliate of Weston Inc. The purchase comes only months after the property appeared headed for demolition. In February, Weston had sought permission to tear down about 183,000 square feet of the remaining factory complex, with the intention of making the site more attractive to a new industrial user.The structures are assessed by Cuyahoga County as being in fair to very poor condition, and the new ownership has begun work to secure and maintain the site. Redevelopment plans are being developed in stages and are expected to cover the entire property.A major project for the new ownerFor Ellis, whose portfolio includes Northeast Ohio development and construction projects, Winton Works represents his largest undertaking to date. Potential tenants have already been identified, although they have not been publicly disclosed. The acquisition also involves TCWB OR LLC, an affiliate of Equity Advantage, which holds a 95% interest alongside Winton Works Ltd.’s 5%. The arrangement is being used for a reverse 1031 exchange, a real estate mechanism that allows an investor to acquire replacement property before selling another asset while potentially deferring capital gains taxes. The immediate priority is bringing the old industrial complex back to a stable, maintained condition before more substantial redevelopment begins.The factory that helped shape the automobileAccording to NEOtrans, the property’s significance goes well beyond its size. Winton Motor Carriage Co. was founded in 1897 by Alexander Winton, a Scottish-born bicycle maker who turned his attention to automobiles. Winton produced Cleveland’s first commercially manufactured automobile in 1898. The company expanded rapidly, and by the beginning of the 20th century its roughly 500,000-square-foot factory was the largest automobile plant in the United States. Winton was also the country’s largest manufacturer of gasoline-powered cars at the time.One of its vehicles completed the first transcontinental automobile journey in 1903, helping establish the company’s reputation during the early years of the American automobile industry. Winton later shifted toward luxury vehicles and diesel engines as mass-produced cars from Henry Ford’s factories changed the economics of the industry. General Motors acquired Winton in 1930, eventually operating the facility as part of its Cleveland Diesel Engine Division before relocating operations elsewhere in 1962.A second life for an industrial landmarkThe factory did not disappear after the automotive era. Over the decades, the property housed a succession of businesses and entertainment venues, including Gair Cleveland Cartons, Superior Wrought Washer, Cleveland Railway, Roman Chariot auto parts and several nightlife establishments. Its latest chapter could be more closely tied to its history. With redevelopment plans taking shape, the goal is no longer simply to clear the land and start over. Preserving the existing buildings offers an opportunity to bring new activity to a piece of Cleveland’s industrial past while retaining the physical character of the original complex.For a property that came close to being reduced to an empty development site, the shift is significant: Winton Works is moving from demolition plans toward a new life built around reuse.Image Courtesy: NEOtransYou use AI every day. Aadhav said TVK’s participation is a formal declaration of it being was part of the alliance.The alliance will hold demonstrations at district headquarters across the state demanding CEC’s removal for “acting unilaterally and unlawfully” during SIR. The parties have alleged that the revision led to the deletion of more than 13 crore voters from electoral rolls.The Chennai demonstration on Oct 15 will bring together TVK, Congress, VCK, CPI, CPM, IUML, MDMK and CPI (ML). articles.summary: India on Friday hit back at Pakistan at the UN General Assembly, rejecting Islamabad’s remarks on Jammu and Kashmir and accusing its “so-called” civilian
articles.body: India on Friday hit back at Pakistan at the UN General Assembly, rejecting Islamabad’s remarks on Jammu and Kashmir and accusing its “so-called” civilian governments of serving “at the mercy” of the army.Exercising its Right of Reply during a Third Committee meeting, first secretary at the Permanent Mission of India to the UN Bhavika Mangalanandan said Pakistan’s civilian governments “rarely complete their terms”, while accusing Islamabad of using cross-border terrorism to divert attention from domestic discontent.Accoridng to news agency PTI, India “categorically” rejected Pakistan’s remarks on Jammu and Kashmir, asserting that the Union Territories of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh were, are and will always remain “integral and inalienable” parts of India.“We all know that the so-called civilian governments in Pakistan serve at the mercy of their army and rarely complete their terms,” Mangalanandan said.Referring to jailed former Pakistan prime minister Imran Khan, she said a “former Prime Minister continues to remain in jail, even as his health is reported to be fast deteriorating.”She also said the erstwhile ruling party had not been allowed to contest elections.“Instead of addressing domestic discontent, Pakistan seeks to distract by fomenting instability in India and sponsoring, inciting, abetting, and financing cross-border terrorism in my country for more than three decades,” she said.Turning to Jammu and Kashmir, Mangalanandan said, “The only outstanding matter is a vacation of the territory Pakistan holds under illegal and forcible occupation.She accused Pakistan of attempting to divert attention from unrest in the country.“This is a desperate attempt by Pakistan to mask the ongoing tragedy in Rawalakot and its other cities, the killing of hundreds of civilians, and the brutal crackdown across Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir, for merely demanding bread, electricity and human dignity,” she said.India also invoked the term “Form 47”, used in reference to allegations of rigging and manipulation in Pakistan’s 2024 general elections.“When any free media is banned from covering such news in Pakistan, the evidence becomes undeniable for the global community that only the writ of the Form 47 government and their masters and the army headquarters runs large,” she said.Contrasting this with Jammu and Kashmir, India said articles.title: A Vietnamese immigrant bought a 23,200-sq-ft White House replica in Georgia; the $35 million mansion has its own Oval Office
articles.summary: A 23,200-square-foot mansion modelled after the White House has gone on the market in Oak Grove, Georgia, for $35 million.
articles.body: A 23,200-square-foot mansion modelled after the White House has gone on the market in Oak Grove, Georgia, for $35 million. The private estate, built in 2001, features a grand exterior inspired by the US presidential residence and rooms designed to echo famous spaces inside it, including an Oval Office-style study. Its current owner, Vietnamese immigrant Thuy Ai Kathy Lam, bought the property in 2013 after building a successful beauty business. She later raised her children there and is now preparing to move to a smaller home.How did a Vietnamese immigrant come to own the 23,200-sq-ft White House replicaLam's connection with this unique property began years before she became its owner. According to Realtor, she moved from postwar Vietnam to Atlanta with her family in 1995. They had only around $200 at the time, and she started working as a nail technician after arriving in the US.Her early years in America were closely tied to the beauty industry. Realtor reported that Lam opened her first nail salon 9 months after arriving, using a loan, and eventually expanded into nail salons and beauty schools. Her business success eventually put the Georgia mansion within reach.The house had already become a familiar sight to her. She remembered passing the White House replica when she was younger and thinking that she would be fortunate even to tour it one day. That changed in 2013, when she and her then-husband, Daniel Nguyen, were looking for a larger home. A joking suggestion that they should buy the property turned into a real conversation, and Lam contacted the owner.The Georgia mansion resembles the real White HouseThe property was built in 2001 by developer Fred Milani, who sent designers to Washington, D.C., to study the original White House before creating the Georgia version. CBS News Atlanta reported that the main residence covers about 16,500 square feet, while Realtor reports the entire estate, including its separate guesthouse, at approximately 23,200 square feet.Its exterior follows the Neoclassical appearance associated with the White House, but the similarities continue inside. One of its most distinctive spaces is an Oval Office-style study. Realtor reported that the room includes a replica of the presidential seal on the ceiling, while the desk resembles the Resolute Desk used in the real Oval Office.Another room takes inspiration from the Lincoln Bedroom. The property also contains formal entertaining spaces, murals, hand-forged iron railings and custom-made furniture. These details give the house its unique connection to the building in Washington without making it an official or public White House property. CBS News stressed that it is a private residence built for personal use.What does the estate include beyond its presidential-style roomsThe scale of the property extends well beyond the main building. The estate sits on roughly 3 acres and includes a separate 7-bedroom guesthouse known as the West Wing. Together, the two residences provide 13 bedrooms.Realtor reported that the main house has 6 bedrooms, while the guesthouse adds seven more. VnExpress reported that the main residence has 11 bathrooms and the guesthouse has another 6. The property therefore provides space for large family gatherings while keeping the two residences separate.The grounds are designed for entertainment as well. VnExpress described manicured gardens, a large swimming pool, a jacuzzi and a pool house with an outdoor kitchen. Inside, the main residence has a dramatic entrance with muralled ceilings, a sweeping staircase and a custom chandelier, along with a home lift.There is also a large banquet hall on the lower level. Realtor reported that it can accommodate about 250 people and has been used for weddings. The guesthouse, meanwhile, has been rented through Airbnb, adding another use to a property that has served as both a family home and an event setting.Why is the White House lookalike now being soldThe $35 million listing marks a new stage for Lam and the property. After more than a decade in the mansion, her children are now in college, and she has decided to move into a smaller home.For Lam, selling the house means giving up a property that became closely connected with her personal story. VnExpress reported that she regarded the mansion as a symbol of her American dream, while Realtor reported her decision as coming after raising her children there. She hopes the next owner will look after the estate as she has done.The mansion has also had a life beyond the Lam family. VnExpress reported that the property has been used as a backdrop for film shoots, family gatherings and special events. Realtor noted that Lam hosted community Christmas parties and a fundraising event there, while tourists and passersby have often stopped to photograph the distinctive building from outside.Significance of the $35 million asking priceAt $35 million, the estate is being offered at a level rarely seen in the Atlanta residential market. Realtor reported that it is the most expensive listing in the Atlanta metropolitan area, while the previous record residential sale stood at $18.1 million in 2021.The property is being represented by Serhant agents Chris Bowes, Tuy Dewey Luong, Annie Tran and Tiffany Powell, according to Realtor. The price reflects more than the home's size. The estate combines a White House-inspired exterior, presidential-style rooms, two residences, extensive grounds and spaces designed for entertaining.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: In 2024, eight watches once owned by Michael Schumacher sold for about CHF 4m; the rarest Ferrari-linked watch reached CHF 1.497m
articles.summary: A remarkable auction of luxury watches once owned by Michael Schumacher, raising around CHF 4 million, including a standout Ferrari-linked timepiece that sold for CHF 1.4 million.
articles.body: Luxury timepieces belonging to seven-time Formula One world champion Michael Schumacher were sold for around CHF 4 million ($4.4 million), as reported by Reuters. Held at the prominent Christie’s auction in Geneva, the high-profile event was organized directly by the racing icon’s family. Collectors from across the Americas bid on the watches. The May 2024 sale was timed to coincide with the 30th anniversary of Schumacher's historic first Formula One Drivers' Championship victory back in 1994.The collection exhibited eight exceptionally rare, custom-built timepieces of renowned global watchmakers such as Rolex, F.P. Journe, and Audemars Piguet. Before hitting the auction, Christie’s gathered momentum for the highly anticipated collection with an international promotional tour, showcasing the timepieces in private gallery viewings in both New York and Taipei.The pre-sale market estimates The Vagabondage 1 model, a custom-made platinum timepiece from watchmaker, F.P. Journe was the standout piece out of the family collection. This unique watch was originally given to the German racing icon as a present for Christmas in 2004 by Jean Todt, his long-time team principal and former CEO at Ferrari. The custom design was defined by an 18-carat white gold framework and a vibrant red watch face along with an engraved emblem of Ferrari, Schumacher's iconic racing helmet, and a symbolic number "7" to honor his championship victories.Landing squarely within its pre-sale estimate, the hammer price reached CHF 1.2 million, rose to CHF 1.497 million (that translates to $1.6 million). Also featured in the auction was a secondary customized watch, an Audemars Piguet Royal Oak chronograph, which was also a piece made for Schumacher from Todt. With the watch's trademark signature of Ferrari’s prancing horse on its dial, it ignited intense bidding, closing at a hammer price of CHF 330,000. It ultimately settled at CHF 415,800 with the buyer's commission. The result beat the pre-sale estimate of CHF 150,000 to 250,000.Global bidding and broader context of the auction According to the Remi Guillemin, what piqued the interest of international collectors was that these items bore historical provenance. While the Head of Watches for Europe and the Americas, didn’t divulge identify any of the individual buyers, he did confirm that a single collector purchased all five distinct watches offered in F.P. Journe's Ruthenium collection boxed set. Besides the custom racing memorabilia, the highest individual payout of the entire event was generated by a vintage pink gold Patek Philippe timepiece, which sold for a price of CHF 2.465 million ($2.71 million).The high-end watch auction faced minor setbacks in the form of logistical complications, owing to which the live bidding process had to be delayed temporarily after the internal digital systems at Christie's suffered a cyber attack. However, the sale continued the following day as part of a broader seasonal auction of rare horological assets in Geneva.Michael Schumacher officially stepped away from professional Formula One racing in 2012 with a resume of seven World Drivers' Championship titles, a record he shares with British driver Lewis Hamilton. A year later on 29 December 2013, the retired athlete fell while skiing off-piste at Méribel in the French Alps and suffered a near-fatal brain injury. Schumacher has since remained elusive to the public and as of 2024 continues to receive private medical care at his family home in Switzerland.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Delhi women’s safety protests: Shivraj Chouhan reacts to viral ‘kachori-samosa’ slogans
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Union minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan has reacted to viral videos from women-led protests in Delhi, questioning why women and girls have been
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Union minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan has reacted to viral videos from women-led protests in Delhi, questioning why women and girls have been forced to raise slogans about their safety and men. The remarks came amid demonstrations following the alleged gang rape of a 17-year-old.Chouhan referred to one of the slogans doing the rounds online, “Ek kachori-do samosa, in mardo ka kya bharosa”, and said the situation required serious consideration.“Why has the situation come to this, that our daughters have to chant slogans like 'One kachori, two samosas'? We must think seriously about this,” he said in a post on X, sharing a video of himself at an event.The protests have also produced a series of rhyming slogans that have spread across social media, including, “Ek kachori, do samosa, in mardon ka kya bharosa,” “1 jeera, 2 ajwain, mard samaj do resign” and “Thandi chai garam karo, mard jaat sharam karo.”The slogans, which have circulated widely through Instagram, X and other platforms, have become part of the online vocabulary around the protests. The demonstrations were triggered by concerns over women’s safety following the alleged gang rape of a 17-year-old at Aastha Kunj Park near Lady Shri Ram College.Chouhan called for a collective commitment to women’s safety and dignity.“We must take a resolve— We will respect our sisters and daughters, we will ensure their safety, and we will protect their rights,” he said.The first major demonstration was held on September 23, when around 200 students from Delhi University and affiliated institutions, including Lady Shri Ram College for Women, Miranda House, Gargi College and Dr BR Ambedkar University, took to the streets.On September 25, hundreds of women students marched near Delhi University’s South Campus, demanding safer public spaces and stronger action against sexual harassment. Another demonstration was later held at the Faculty of Arts.The protests have since been followed by measures from civic and security agencies. The Delhi Development Authority and Municipal Corporation of Delhi undertook safety audits of public parks, focusing on lighting, security personnel at entry and exit points and patrolling after sundown. Delhi Police also stepped up patrolling across parks and other areas.All three accused in the Aastha Kunj case have been arrested, according to PTI. One accused was pursuing a law course, whole another was arrested after an encounter with a Delhi Police.The issue has also drawn political reactions. Lok Sabha Leader of the Opposition Rahul Gandhi backed the student-led protests and said, “Stop punishing women for the crimes committed against them. Across our country, women are afraid to walk the streets, afraid of being harassed, afraid of being raped. And the government’s answer: stay at home,” Gandhi said.Former Delhi chief minister Arvind Kejriwal also questioned restrictions placed on women, while chief minister Rekha Gupta said women’s safety should not come at the cost of restricting their freedom.Gupta said the Delhi government was strengthening safety infrastructure, including 50,000 CCTV cameras and one lakh streetlights.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: A 1987 Buick GNX, No. 450 of just 547 built for a single model year, sold for $200,000 with 26 miles in 2024; two years and only 4 miles later, the 30-mile car sold again for $427,000
articles.summary: Some cars age and others simply become more expensive to own.
articles.body: Some cars age and others simply become more expensive to own. A 1987 Buick GNX with barely 30 miles on its odometer has demonstrated just how dramatically collector demand can shift, selling for $427,000 after changing hands for $200,000 only two years earlier, states an online report by Bring A Trailer. The black performance coupe, number 450 of just 547 GNXs built for the model year, has covered only four additional miles since its previous sale, adds the online report.From $200,000 to $427,000According to September 2026 report by Bring A Trailer, the GNX previously sold on Bring a Trailer in July 2024 with 26 miles on the odometer. It has since been acquired by the dealer now offering the car in Texas, with the mileage increasing to just 30 miles. The latest transaction more than doubled the car's previous sale price, highlighting the premium attached to exceptionally preserved examples of one of the most sought-after American performance cars of the 1980s.The car comes with manufacturer literature, memorabilia, copies of its original window sticker, a clean Carfax report and a clean California title, adds the report.Built to end the Grand National eraThe Grand National Experimental, or GNX, was developed as a final celebration of Buick's Grand National production run. Buick partnered with McLaren Performance Technologies and ASC to turn the already formidable Grand National into a limited-production performance model. Only 547 examples were produced, all in black, making the cars instantly recognizable. The GNX added a collection of visual and mechanical upgrades, including composite wheel-arch flares, heat-extracting fender vents, GNX badging, sport mirrors, dual exhaust outlets and a distinctive three-piece rear spoiler, reads the online report. The car also rides on 16-inch cross-lace wheels and features a limited-slip differential, air conditioning and cruise control.A turbocharged V6 with serious muscleIf we go by the report, under the hood is a turbocharged 3.8-liter V6 modified by ASC/McLaren. The engine received a Garrett T3 turbocharger, a larger air-to-air intercooler and a lower-restriction exhaust system. Factory output was rated at 276 horsepower and 360 lb-ft of torque. Power reaches the rear wheels through a 200R4 four-speed automatic transmission fitted with an upgraded oil cooler. A GNX-branded aluminum cover distinguishes the limited-slip differential at the rear.The suspension was also reworked and the GNX retained front suspension components from the contemporary Grand National while gaining upgraded rear hardware, including a Panhard rod, torque arm and additional frame crossmember. Power-assisted front disc brakes and rear drums handle stopping duties.Preserved almost exactly as deliveredInside, the GNX remains unmistakably rooted in its era. A three-spoke leather-wrapped steering wheel sits ahead of GNX-specific Stewart-Warner instrumentation. The instrument cluster includes a 160-mph speedometer, an 8,000-rpm tachometer and dedicated gauges monitoring turbo boost, oil pressure, coolant temperature and fuel level. The five-digit odometer now reads just 30 miles, making the car less a used performance machine than a remarkably preserved snapshot of Buick's brief but significant assault on the American performance-car market.Why the GNX remains collectibleThe GNX arrived at the end of an era when turbocharged American cars were beginning to challenge expectations about what a large domestic coupe could do. Its limited production, McLaren-developed mechanical upgrades and distinctive appearance have since made it a cornerstone of 1980s performance-car collecting. For this particular example, the jump from $200,000 to $427,000 in just two years, and with only four additional miles, adds another chapter to that collector story.Image Courtesy: Bring A TrailerYou use AI every day. articles.title: In England, a retired teacher spent decades filling his one-bedroom flat with handmade miniature towns, barns and memory boxes built from his travels with his wife
articles.summary: Ken Bonham, a retired teacher from Birmingham, has dedicated decades to crafting intricate miniature barns and travel memory boxes, showcasing his passion for architecture and travel memorabilia within his one-bedroom flat.
articles.body: There’s a private universe of miniature architecture and geographical dioramas to be found in the one-bedroom flat of a retired teacher in Birmingham. Spanning over decades, the collection of 79-year-old Ken Bonham has grown to include numerous historical models, travel-themed memory displays, and Christmas holiday installations made by hand. The collection includes historic barn replicas, card models, and memory boxes.As per Miniatura, the residential collection is centered around specialized architectural niches realized through a gamut of historic European threshing barns captured in precise 1:100 scale miniatures. Bonham started the study of these structures following his retirement from a career of teaching primary school students through to adults. Bonham was conducting an educational IT consultancy course in Bristol, joined by his wife of 54 years, Maggie. The couple decided to take a geographical detour to visit the historic Ashleworth Tithe Barn and Middle Littleton Tithe Barn. This established a project of active "barn hunting," which he had pursued for 12 years by 2021, across the United Kingdom and continental Europe.From structural fieldwork to precision engineering To maintain structural ingenuity, Bonham relies on extensive research that he himself catalogued and documented about 400 barns. His creative itinerary includes European landmarks such as the great barn at Ter Doest near Bruges and numerous barns in the open-air museums in Bokrijk and Arnhem as per Miniatura . To fit these structures into his flat while ensuring their transportability for educational lectures, Bonham uses a strict 1:100 engineering scale because building a 200-foot threshing barn at a standard 1:24 scale would result in a massive model of roughly eight feet and prove entirely impractical for his living space.Each model is constructed in a way that is emblematic of the historical carpentry techniques of the original structures. Using his own photographs, diagrams, and plans where available, he makes interior roof trusses beforehand from balsa wood and assembles the frameworks bay by bay. Other materials such as cork, card, and clay form the exterior walls.How the memory boxes are made Moving beyond agricultural structures, the flat houses a gamut of detailed travel dioramas, which he calls "memory boxes" or "memento boxes." The purpose of these boxes was to permanently preserve physical artifacts collected during excursions. Since then whenever they traveled, they salvaged those memories by collecting postcards, tickets to museums, iconic figures which Bonham catalogued and arranged into a box. Some of these hang on the wall, and some are freestanding on a shelf.The Guardian reports he made one box about their visits to Paris and another about their trip by train through the south of France to Avignon. The Irish trip had Celtic crosses, card models that Bonham made from his photographic records of Celtic monasteries, model Celtic stones, and a scale model of Trinity College Dublin. Additional contents also included a miniature bottle of Guinness and a souvenir representing historic Georgian doorways in Dublin.A larger British box, measuring four feet high by three feet wide, contains toy cars and vintage model soldiers from his childhood. There was also sand gathered from beaches, England's Glory matchboxes, a telephone box, a transport bus from London and one figure of a Royal Lifeboat man. Together, these boxes and barns form a lasting record of Bonham's travels, kept within the walls of his Birmingham flat.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Airport access fee may push up cab fares
articles.summary: Thiruvananthapuram airport introduces access fees for commercial cabs, potentially raising taxi fares; charges aim to cut congestion and boost revenue.
articles.body: T’puram: Cab fares from the city airport may increase as the airport began charging an access fee for commercial vehicles or cabs picking up passengers from the arrival terminal.Under the revised tariff, cabs are charged Rs 180 for entering the arrival terminal pick-up zone for eight minutes. The charge increases to Rs 200 for up to 30 minutes if the vehicle stays beyond eight minutes.There is concern that cab operators may pass on the additional cost to passengers hiring taxis from the airport.Commercial vehicles dropping passengers at the departure terminal will be charged Rs 50 for up to eight minutes and Rs 200 for up to 30 minutes.Private vehicles, however, will not be charged for stays of up to eight minutes. They will be charged Rs 150 under the next 30-minute slab if they exceed the time limit.Entry and exit at the airport are smoother than at airports in major cities, allowing cabs to leave within eight minutes.Still, the Rs 180 charge would impose an additional burden on commercial vehicle operators, who may have to spend a significant portion of their earnings—nearly 50% of the fare from a trip in some cases—on the airport fee.M K Ajit Kumar, a frequent traveller, said that the access fee charged is not a huge amount for someone who takes a flight. “The cab operator may transfer it to the passenger. But it is not too high. But the airport should also ensure security of passengers by ensuring that the vehicles that come to pick up are safe for the people.”An airport official said that the charges have been increased as part of efforts to reduce congestion at the terminal and improve non-aeronautical revenue. articles.title: Delay in induction of fighter jets hurting us, we need 36-40 aircraft annually: IAF chief; says Pak buying & training its pilots on Chinese stealth jets ‘cause for worry’
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Indian Air Force chief Air Chief Marshal Amar Preet Singh said on Saturday the delay in the induction of fighter jets is “hurting us as our
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Indian Air Force chief Air Chief Marshal Amar Preet Singh said on Saturday the delay in the induction of fighter jets is “hurting us as our (squadron) numbers have gone down especially after the phase-out of MiG-21s..., and we need to plug this gap by adding 36-40 aircraft annually” for the next few years. However, the IAF chief made it clear that “we have less numbers, but we are not weak.”Addressing his last press conference as IAF chief, ACM Singh, who is scheduled to superannuate on Oct 31, said, “It happens that you plan something, but things get delayed. But this time, the delay has been long. I reiterate what I said earlier, ‘technology delayed is technology denied’. The IAF’’s fighter squadrons have depleted to an alarming 29 from an ideal 42.5. He said that keeping the challenging situation for the country, the IAF actually needs more than 42 squadrons.About the proposed induction of jets, the IAF chief said, “We are also looking towards multi-role fighter aircraft (MRFA), LCA MK1A and proposed Mark-2. All these will be able to fill the gaps that exist now and in future (as some more fighters will be phased out). Also, we have 5th-generation fighter jet programme AMCA, we have to see how it progresses... We are giving our full support.. If there are delays in it, we have to make some other decisions,” Singh said.On the proposed deal of 114 Rafale jets with France, IAF chief said the multirole fighter aircraft contract is likely to be signed by this financial year. He said Russia has offered India Su-57 fifth-generation fighter jets but no decision has been made on it.Singh said reports of Pakistan acquiring Chinese fifth-generation stealth fighters and training its pilots in China are a “cause for worry”. Pakistan is reportedly set to acquire up to 40 Chinese J-35A stealth fighter jets, marking China's first-ever export of a fifth-generation combat aircraft.He said Pakistan failed to do much in Operation Sindoor despite having various platforms as their integration was not done. This proves that integration of various platforms matters the most, he said. On modernisation of the IAF, he said the force has to be augmented through artificial intelligence. "We have to have an AI-augmented force," he said.About the make-in-India initiative, the IAF chief, ahead of 94th Air Force Day, said, “Atmanirbharta is a necessity. But we can’t have atmanirbharata at the cost of our defence preparedness. Atmanirbharata can’t happen overnight. The whole ecosystem has to be created. If I am asked whether we are moving in the right direction, yes we are. But I am not the right person to ask whether it is moving at the right pace.”Talking about theatrisation, he said, “IAF is not against theatre commands. But we have a new situation after Op Sindoor and we should look at all aspects before taking the final decision.”Singh ruled out creating a separate drone force, saying unmanned systems and loitering munitions should remain integrated with the IAF’s existing weapons and platforms. He described drones as an “evolutionary” capability for the force and said their numbers, types and operational use are being expanded.“Military power becomes the ultimate, and without adequate military power, any state remains vulnerable to coercion, and if we have to do things our way, if we have to follow the path that we want to follow, we have to have a strong military. “And when we talk about a strong military, in the recent conflicts we have seen that it is the air power which has come to the fore, which has come out as the cutting edge of military power, and it is one instrument on which any nation relies to meet its objectives,” he said.“Whether we look at defence transactions worldwide and strategic conversations that are taking place — whether it is advanced fighter aircraft, long-range precision weapons, integrated air command and control, or unmanned aerial systems — it is all very clear that they all reflect that military power is concentrated around the aerospace domain," the IAF chief.Singh credits the entire force for its recent achievements. “No individual is bigger than the institution.” However, he said he is ready to take a blame personally for any shortcomings as the head of the organisation.The IAF chief praised Indian pilot Smit Machchhar who recently saved the lives of 174 passengers despite being stabbed by his co-pilot in the flydubai incident. “What our Indian pilot has done is exceptionally great. He showed presence of mind, physical resolve, and mental resolve. It is also a lesson for us,” he said.

articles.body: Raipur: A special Gram Sabha in Punpalli village of Sukma has passed a resolution saying no Gram Sabha land will be made available to Christians or converts for burials, churches, prayer meetings or “healing” gatherings, and has also put up a public notice barring pastors and Christian preachers from entering the village for conversion or religious activity.The resolution, passed as decision number 6 of the special Gram Sabha, cites Article 244(1) of the Constitution, the fifth schedule, the Panchayats (extension to scheduled areas) Act, 1996, and Chhattisgarh’s PESA framework to justify the move, confirmed Bheema Markam, the janpad member.The notice erected at the entrance of the village states that not “an inch” of Gram Sabha land would be given for burial of Christian or converted persons, churches, prayer meetings or healing gatherings.It also says pastors, priests and Christian preachers would not be allowed to enter Punpalli for conversion, prayer meetings or related religious activity.Janpad member Madkam Bhima said the Gram Sabha had taken the decision keeping in mind the village’s traditional system, social unity and community interests, while adding that any dispute should be dealt with through legal and constitutional processes.The development is significant because Punpalli lies in a Scheduled Area, where PESA gives Gram Sabhas substantial powers to safeguard tribal traditions, customs, cultural identity, community resources and customary methods of dispute resolution. The central PESA Act explicitly recognises those powers.However, the Act does not expressly state that a Gram Sabha can exclude people from community land or village religious life solely on the basis of their faith. That makes the scope and legal enforceability of Punpalli’s resolution a potentially contentious question.The issue is particularly sensitive in Bastar, where disputes over conversion, burial rights and the religious identity of tribal communities have repeatedly led to confrontation.In January 2025, the supreme court had to intervene in a Chhattisgarh burial dispute after a Christian tribal family from Bastar said it was prevented from burying a deceased family member in the village. The case highlighted the tension between local customary claims, burial practices and constitutional rights.Punpalli’s special Gram Sabha said its decision was aimed at protecting the village’s cultural identity, traditional practices and social heritage. The resolution has been displayed publicly on an information board so residents and visitors are aware of it.Among those present at the Gram Sabha were sarpanch Sonmati Madvi, Gram Sabha president Barse Soma, deputy sarpanch Muchaki Nanda, village Patel Barse Pandu and other traditional and elected representatives.Officials said the administration would examine the Gram Sabha resolution and the notice put up in Punpalli to determine whether the decisions fall within the powers available to a Gram Sabha under PESA and other applicable laws.They said Gram Sabhas in Scheduled Areas have an important role in protecting customary practices, traditions and community resources.“The contents of the resolution and the circumstances in which it was passed will be looked into. articles.title: In 2022, engineers mixed recycled textile fabric into cement; after accelerated aging, the silica-fume composite kept its flexural strength and retained post-crack performance
articles.summary: A groundbreaking study reveals the strength and durability of cement composites reinforced with recycled textile fabric and silica fume, showing retained performance even after artificial aging.
articles.body: Engineers in 2022, tested a cement based composite reinforced with flax and recycled fabric waste, containing 30% silica fume, and found that it kept its pre-aging flexural performance after aging. The treated composite recorded between 14.3 and 15.4 MPa in flexural strength, while its toughness ranged from 8.1 to 8.7 kJ/m². The study, titled “Microstructural Properties of Hybrid Textile Waste-Flax Fabric-Reinforced Cement Composites,”explored whether the integration of recycled textile fibers into cement-based materials could solve durability issues found in natural fibers. The researchers produced a nonwoven fabric consisting of 65% recycled textile-waste fibers and 35% flax fibers.In its final composition, the fabric contained about 45% cotton and 20% polyester from the recycled portion, plus 35% flax. By using six layers of hybrid fabric, the researchers reinforced the cement-based composite. They substituted portions of the Portland cement matrix with silica fume at three distinct levels: 0%, to 15%, and 30%. Following production, the composites underwent testing for flexural and tensile performance under unaged conditions, as well as after accelerated wet-dry and freeze-thaw cycles.Silica fume reduced fibre degradation during accelerated aging The study found that wet-dry cycles had a greater effect on the textile-reinforced composites as opposed to freeze-thaw cycles. The flexural strength of the composite without silica fume fell from 16.5 MPa in the unaged condition to 10.0 MPa after wet-dry ageing, marking a reduction of 40%. Conversely, the composite containing 30% silica exhibited a different behaviour. Its strength measured 14.5 MPa before aging, after wet-dry cycles it was 14.3 MPa, and 15.4 MPa after freeze-thaw cycles. Consequently, the researchers determined that the 30% silica fume composite maintained similar performance across all tested conditions.In case of flexural toughness the results were almost the same: without silica fumes, toughness fell from 10.1 kJ/m² in the unaged condition to 6.5 kJ/m² after wet-dry cycles, indicating a loss of more than 35%. With 30% silica fume, toughness dipped only slightly, which limited the loss to about 5%. Researchers attributed this to the effect of silica fume on the matrix cement through their X-ray diffraction and thermogravimetric analysis, which revealed that the amount of calcium hydroxide in the matrix is reduced by increasing silica fume. Calcium hydroxide was reduced by almost 66% in the 30% silica fume sample when compared to the sample without silica fume. This minimized the alkaline conditions responsible for the degradation and embrittlement of the fibers during accelerated aging.Recycled textile fabric continued to contribute after cracking The main objective of the textile reinforcement was to improve the material’s behaviour after the cement matrix cracked. During flexural testing, the fibers transferred tensile stresses across cracks, which allowed the composite to sustain load and develop multiple instead of failing immediately after the first crack.After aging the material's post-cracking behavior became especially prominent. Under wet-dry cycles, the stiffness within the composite without silica fume degraded by more than 60%. Conversely, under the same conditions, for the composite with 30% silica fume the reduction was only 20%. Furthermore, when subjected to freeze-thaw cycles, the stiffness reduction for the 30% silica fume composite was limited to 7%.Tests for direct tensile showed the same effects, under the wet dry cycles the tensile strength of the composite without silica fume and the 30% silica fume composite was reduced by 50% and 15% respectively. Further microscopic examination confirmed that after wet-dry aging, fibers in the composite without silica fume suffered greater degradation whereas most fibers in the 30% silica fume composite retained their length after failure with degradation. The researchers concluded that when the cement matrix is modified with 30% silica fume, it prevents significant fiber embrittlement and retains flexural and post-cracking properties more effectively under wet-dry and freeze-thaw conditions, supporting its potential use in building components.You use AI every day. articles.title: Pisces, Weekly Horoscope, October 04 to October 10, 2026: Steady discipline and supportive connections bring brighter progress and financial gains
articles.summary: General: This week begins with a bright and capable mood, Pisces.
articles.body: General:This week begins with a bright and capable mood, Pisces. The early stretch suits learning, work, practical responsibilities, and even a little public visibility. If you have been waiting for the right moment to push a project, submit an application, or sort out a pending task, the opening days are helpful. Employees can handle duties neatly, and students may feel mentally sharp. A family event or social gathering may also pull you out of routine and remind you that life is not only about deadlines and duty. For businesspersons, travel or long-distance communication may become a strong theme, and those efforts can support future growth. If you play sports or compete in any field, there may be recognition that boosts your confidence.The middle of the week keeps the momentum going. You are active, cheerful, and mentally alert. In some ways, this is your strongest window, because confidence rises without becoming arrogant. Still, later in the week the current changes. A little fog enters the picture. Health may wobble, pressure from opponents or jealous people can increase, and you may realise that not every plan should be spoken aloud. That's not a reason to become fearful, only wiser. Hold your cards close. If someone keeps prying into your next move, smile and move on.The week closes on a warm, human note. Family comfort, romance, supportive partnership, and simple joys become more important than outer noise. There may be a picnic, outing, or pleasant time spent with loved ones. Unmarried Pisces may hear of a proposal through known people. By Saturday, your partner's support can become the best medicine for the week's strain. It is a week like a river after rain, lively at first, a little muddy for a day, then calm and reflective by the banks again.Love and Relationships:Your heart is in good shape this week, and that shows in the way you speak, listen, and respond. Early in the week, love has an easy rhythm. If you are seeing someone, Tuesday in particular can feel lucky. Conversations flow, affection feels natural, and you may find it easier than usual to say what you mean without overthinking every word. This is helpful for Pisces, because you often feel first and explain later. Let your warmth show. It will be well received.By Friday, relationships become one of the happiest parts of the week. Family time looks cheerful, and some of you may enjoy an outing, a picnic, or a simple shared meal that turns memorable because everyone is in a good mood. If you're unmarried, a marriage offer may arrive through relatives, family friends, or a trusted network. If you're in love, this is a strong time to express your feelings clearly. No need for grand poetry unless that's your style. Even a direct, sincere sentence can change the atmosphere. Giving a thoughtful gift to your spouse or partner will go far now, not because of money, but because it shows attention.Saturday deepens emotional support. Your life partner or close companion may stand firmly by your side, especially if the latter half of the week leaves you tired or irritated. Romance grows from care, not performance. Do remember one thing during Thursday's tense patch. Don't carry suspicion into your closest bonds. Hidden enemies are one matter, but your loved ones are not the enemy. Be respectful, especially in your tone with women and elders. A week like this can gently remind you that the safest place in your life is often the person who already knows your worries and stays anyway.Education and Career:This is a good working week, especially for those who begin with a plan instead of waiting for motivation to appear. Monday, Tuesday, and Wednesday are productive for study, office work, training, writing, and practical execution. Students can make real progress if they sit down properly and use these days rather than merely feeling hopeful about them. Educational matters show success, and if you're preparing for tests, interviews, or presentations, your memory and expression can support you well. Employees may feel especially confident around midweek, and routine duties can be completed with less friction than usual.Businesspersons have a bolder current running through the week. Tuesday supports brave decisions, and Wednesday can bring long-distance movement, new contacts, or travel linked to future profit. If you work in sales, supply, consulting, or anything that grows through outreach, these are useful days for calls, meetings, and proposals. Athletes and performers can also do well now, especially where discipline meets public recognition. The effort you have put in quietly may begin to show visible results.Thursday is the caution zone. Keep your strategy private. Don't discuss exam plans, office politics, or business intentions too freely. Competitive exams are favoured, yes, but that doesn't mean you should become careless. Rivals or critics may try to create pressure, and arguments will only drain your concentration. Service-class individuals may not see dramatic change this week, but consistency itself will protect your progress. By Saturday, studies regain support and business collaborations can become useful. Read the room. Act with confidence early, act with discretion later. That's how you'll get the best out of this week.Money and Finance:Your financial picture this week is mixed in an encouraging way. There are openings to gain, but only if you avoid impulsive mistakes. Early in the week, spending may go towards family events, travel, social commitments, or small comforts. None of that looks harmful by itself. In fact, some of it may be necessary and worthwhile. Tuesday can favour speculative activity for some of you, especially if you are already informed and disciplined. This is not a free pass to throw money around. It simply suggests that calculated risk may work better than usual for a brief period.Midweek continues to support progress through business movement and confidence. Long-distance work, travel, or expansion plans may plant seeds for future earnings. Yet by Thursday, the tone changes sharply. Do not borrow money unless absolutely unavoidable. Repayment can become heavier than expected. Also, don't share your financial ideas or upcoming decisions with every cousin, colleague, or friend who asks. Loose talk can attract interference or comparison. If someone pressures you into a joint financial move, step back and think.The weekend brings a more conservative money mood. Friday offers pleasure through family time and personal bonding, but health expenses or small comfort spending may rise if you are not paying attention. Saturday is better for saving than risking. New business collaborations may look useful and profitable over time, while speculation should be set aside. Keep records clean. Check digital payments, subscriptions, and recurring expenses. A little discipline now will make you feel safer later. Think of your finances like a clay pot filled drop by drop. It doesn't become full in one dramatic moment. It fills because you remembered not to spill.Health and Well-being:Your health begins the week on a fairly steady note. Energy is decent, the mood is cheerful, and you can get through your routine without dragging yourself. This is a helpful time to establish basic order, proper meals, enough water, regular sleep, and at least a little movement. You needn't turn into a fitness fanatic by Tuesday morning. Just don't neglect the body while chasing work or social plans. A stable system will support all the other good signs showing this week.Wednesday still feels active and enthusiastic, but Thursday asks for care. You may not feel entirely well, and the drop can be linked as much to mental pressure as to physical causes. Stress from competition, comparison, or hidden tension can show up as fatigue, restlessness, poor digestion, or general discomfort. Don't disclose your weaknesses to people who misuse information, but do take practical care of yourself. If you are appearing for an exam or handling pressure at work, build in breaks. Your body is not a machine.Friday and Saturday ask for gentle attention, especially regarding internal health and urinary issues for some Pisces natives. Don't ignore unusual discomfort. Keep your meals light if your system feels overloaded, and stay hydrated through the day. Saturday also favours a better fitness routine, so even a short stretch session, a walk after dinner, or getting back to your usual exercise can help. Emotional well-being improves through affectionate company. Time with your spouse, partner, or family can calm your nerves more quickly than solitary brooding. This week, wellness comes not from force, but from kind habits repeated quietly.Get the latest astrology news and horoscope updates. Reuters reported that police also confirmed they had concluded searches at two London properties linked to the investigation.The investigation into the incident near the military base is underway, police said.The latest arrest follows the detention of five British men, all in their 20s, near three suspicious vans close to RAF Fairford last weekend. articles.title: Will take steps to address gaps in child adoption mechanism, central agency tells Kerala HC
articles.summary: CARA tells Kerala HC it will review Adoption Regulations 2022 to fix gaps, curb repeated child placements, consider ombudsman/board, and ensure post-dissolution support.
articles.body: Kochi: The Central Adoption Resource Authority (Cara) has informed the high court that it would examine measures to address gaps in safeguards under the existing child adoption mechanism, including restricting multiple replacements of a child and establishing an annulment review board or an adoption ombudsman.Cara deputy director Richa Ojha made the submissions in response to a report filed by the victim rights centre (VRC) of the Kerala Legal Services Authority (KeLSA), suggesting amendments to the Adoption Regulations, 2022, with a focus on strengthening safeguards for children during and after adoption. The case arose from a petition filed by a single parent who had adopted a child and sought permission to surrender the child, citing the child’s mental ailment.In a counter affidavit filed by Ojha on behalf of Cara, it was stated that several recommendations made by the VRC were already addressed, fully or substantially, under the existing statutory framework of the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015. However, certain suggestions, including restricting multiple placements of a child and establishing an annulment review board or an adoption ombudsman, would be examined as part of the ongoing review and amendment of the Adoption Regulations, 2022.Regarding the restriction on repeated placement of a child from one family to another, the VRC stated that such placements could disrupt a child’s sense of security, continuity and belonging. It recommended that foster care should be clearly understood as temporary unless converted into a permanent arrangement, and that foster families should receive adequate financial, social, counselling and professional support. Cara, in its reply, stated that the issue was partially addressed, with Regulation 9(4) barring adoptive parents responsible for disruption or dissolution from adopting again. However, no specific provision presently prescribes a limit on repeated re-placement of a child in foster care.Similarly, the VRC suggested a multidisciplinary annulment review board with mandatory representation from Cara and its state counterpart, or an adoption ombudsman, which should exhaust alternatives such as counselling, respite foster care or mediation before allowing disruption or dissolution. Cara replied that the suggestion would be examined during the ongoing review and amendment of the regulations.In another major recommendation, the VRC proposed that financial support for the child should continue following dissolution. Subject to applicable law, adoptive parents should continue to bear responsibility for the child’s financial, educational, medical and other essential needs, ensuring continuity of care, stability, dignity and protection from sudden financial deprivation following termination of the adoptive relationship. Cara replied that specific provisions to secure the child’s financial interests by adoptive parents in cases of annulment or dissolution were under active consideration.The recommendations also include clarifying the role of specialised adoption agencies in dissolution proceedings, strengthening the role of legal services institutions and strengthening pre-adoption preparation of children, among other measures.
